missing: Per-device placement on the real topology, not a pool total. The Phase 1 topology exports only `-d Vulkan0` on workers, and R03-F8 says ggml-rpc-server exposes a CPU device only when a node has no accelerator; so the remotely addressable memory is the measured free VRAM (S-02: ahnoway 7577 + optiplex 5568 + hub 4247 MiB = 17.4 GiB / 18.2 GB) plus the hub's own CPU RAM (16 GB total, ~12 GB available, 8 GB under the Phase-1 exception). Qwen3.8-27B Q8_0 (~29.3 GB at 8k) therefore needs ~12-14 GB outside VRAM, more than the hub can give. Missing: (a) whether `ggml-rpc-server -d Vulkan0,CPU` (or a second instance) can export a worker's host RAM at b10581, and how llama-server's free-memory split weighs a remote CPU device (it will read the worker's whole free RAM and pull layers into slow RAM unless `-ts` overrides); (b) the per-device GB and layer counts for Q8_0 and each backup on this fleet, the recommended `-ts` vector with the device order (RPC devices are not shown by `--list-devices --rpc`, S-03), and whether `-ngl 99` vs `-ngl auto` (fit_params, R03-F11) puts the remainder on CPU or aborts when weights exceed device memory; (c) the exception request S-04 should make (the spec's 7/5/3.5 GB VRAM and 10/12/8 GB RAM figures were not derived from any R04 arithmetic).

'Fits the ~81 GB pool' is computed against total RAM, not usable memory. Available RAM is ~12 (hub) + 19 (optiplex) + ~10 (ahnoway) = ~41 GB, and the Phase-1 exception budget is 15.5 GB VRAM + 30 GB RAM = 45.5 GB. The dossier should state which >=25 GB candidates fit 45.5 GB (Qwen3.8 Q8_0 29.3, Muse Glimmer Q8_0 29.8, Gemma 4 Q8_0 35.1, Llama/DeepSeek 70B IQ3_XXS 30.2 and Q3_K_M 36.9 yes; 70B IQ4_XS 40.6 marginal; 70B Q4_K_M 45.2 and gpt-oss-120b 63.7 no) and which fit the GPU-only topology of the spec (none), so the plan writer knows a topology or cap decision is a prerequisite of the thesis run.

Smoke-test arithmetic is wrong. Rec 5 says Qwen3.8-27B Q4_K_M 18.97 GB + ~0.5 GB KV 'fits 8+4+6 = 18 GB of VRAM without touching CPU RAM'; 19.5 GB exceeds both the 18.2 GB measured free VRAM and the 15.5 GB granted under the demo exceptions, before compute buffers. Needed: a smoke-test quant that genuinely fits measured free VRAM under the caps (e.g. unsloth UD-Q4_K_M 16.46 GB, bartowski Q4_K_S 16.71 GB, UD-Q3_K_XL 13.15 GB, bartowski IQ3_XXS 12.63 GB) with KV and per-device compute buffers included in the sum.

No overhead beyond weights + KV is estimated or measured for any candidate: per-device compute/graph buffers, the logits buffer (n_ubatch x 248,320 x 4 B ~0.5 GB at n_ubatch 512), the 248,320 x 5,120 token-embedding (~1.3 GB at Q8_0) that R03-F12 says always stays on the host CPU, Vulkan context overhead, and what the hub's mmap page cache does under `MemoryMax=8G` while it streams a 28.6 GB file to workers. No `llama-server` load-log lines ('KV self size', 'compute buffer size') exist for the chosen model (one local load of Q4_K_M on ahnoway would give them). Also unknown: how many slots `-np -1` (auto) creates at b10581 and whether `-c 8192` with `--kv-unified` is one 8k cache or several. Without this the marginal picks (UD-Q6_K_XL 26.0, Mistral Small Q8_0 26.4, Qwen3-30B-A3B Q6_K 25.9 GB) cannot be classified, and the `-ctk/-ctv q8_0` variant (halves KV) is unquantified.

'Impossible on one node' is not yet a testable exit condition. llama.cpp mmaps by default and will load a 29 GB GGUF on a 25 GB node by paging from disk (slow, not failing); the dossier gives no operational test (e.g. `--no-mmap`/`--mlock` load on optiplex failing, or resident VRAM+RSS exceeding physical memory, or a tok/s floor). It also does not state that the 25 GB ceiling depends on optiplex's ~13 GB production footprint: against optiplex's total 6.4 GB VRAM + 32 GB RAM = 38 GB, Qwen3.8 Q8_0 (29.3) and Muse Glimmer (29.8) would fit one idle node, while Gemma 4 Q8_0 (35.1, marginal), the 70B at >= Q3_K_M (36.9+) and gpt-oss-120b exceed it. The ADR needs this caveat to make the thesis claim robust, or needs to pick a candidate that clears 38 GB.

Thinking/reasoning control for the demo is absent. Qwen3.8-27B ships with thinking on by default (F17) and Gemma 4 31B's AA score is the '(Reasoning)' variant. Missing: the b10581 llama-server flags or chat-template kwargs to disable or budget thinking (`--reasoning-budget`, `--chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":false}'`, `--reasoning-format`), whether the built-in web UI renders reasoning, and whether the acceptance curl with `max_tokens: 96` returns non-empty `content` when thinking is on (it may spend all 96 tokens on reasoning). Also how Artificial Analysis's 'xhigh' effort setting maps (or does not) to anything llama.cpp exposes, and which of the card's sampling defaults (F15: temp 0.7 / top_p 0.8 / top_k 20 / presence 1.5 instruct; 1.0 / 0.95 / 20 / 0 thinking) the server unit should pass.

Backend support per candidate at the pinned build is unaddressed for Vulkan. Phase 1 runs the Vulkan tarball b10581 on all three GPUs including a Maxwell GTX 970; R04-F48 only discusses CUDA/RPC. Missing: whether the Vulkan backend at b10581 implements the Gated-DeltaNet/recurrent ops of Qwen3.8-27B (and Qwen3.6, Nemotron's Mamba) and the sliding-window paths of Muse Glimmer / Gemma 4, or whether unsupported ops fall back to the host CPU (changing placement and tok/s); whether ggml-rpc's supports_op passes them for remote devices; and the first llama.cpp tag supporting each architecture (qwen3_5 with Qwen3.8's 248,320 vocab and MTP tensors, muse_glimmer, gemma4, NemotronH) so the plan can confirm the pin is new enough. Note the dossier recommends 'v0.2.0' while R03-F1 shows v0.2.0 = b10566, fifteen builds older than the b10581 the spec pinned.

No tokens/s expectation for any candidate, even a memory-bandwidth back-of-envelope. With ~12-14 GB of a dense 27B sitting in the hub's DDR3 RAM (i5-4690K, 4 threads, roughly 20-25 GB/s) the decode floor is ~1-2 tok/s regardless of RPC, and S-03 showed tg 457 -> 94 t/s over RPC even for a 135M model. MoE candidates (Qwen3-30B-A3B-2507 Q8_0 32.5 GB / 3B active, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B-A3B Q8_0 33.6 GB) read ~10x fewer bytes per token. The dossier ranks on AA only; the plan cannot trade 'wow per GB' against 'a friend waits three minutes' without a per-candidate estimate of prompt-processing vs generation speed and where attention vs DeltaNet layers land.

The fallback list is prose, unranked, and incomplete. The '> 8 GB VRAM but < 25 GB' set (section 4) lacks weights + KV at 4k/8k and AA scores, and offers nothing for the case where worker CPU export proves unusable and only ~15.5 GB VRAM is addressable (e.g. Qwen3.8-27B UD-Q3_K_XL 13.1 GB, gpt-oss-20b 12.1 GB, or the smaller Apache-2.0 sizes of Qwen3.6 / Gemma 4 that were not surveyed). The plan needs one ranked table: model, quant, bytes, KV 4k/8k, total, AA score, licence, fits-VRAM-under-caps yes/no.

Verification status of what the spec cites. F19 (the chosen model's KV and recurrent-state arithmetic) is author-flagged UNVERIFIED and F20-F39 (every backup's licence, sizes and KV) are beyond the refutation cap. In particular the section-4 rows for Muse-Glimmer-30B ('Meta Superintelligence Lab' under the unusual HF org `meta-models`; USAGE_POLICY.md in the official GGUF repo never read), Gemma 4's Apache-2.0 claim (F23) and the 70B distill's dual licence (F30/F32) are unverified. The dossier should say which of these a plan may cite as-is and which need a refutation pass before a CLAUDE.md section-4 row is committed.

File identity and attribution details for the commit that downloads the model: SHA-256 (HF LFS oid) of Qwen3.8-27B-Q8_0.gguf and Q4_K_M.gguf are not recorded (the plan runs `sha256sum` but has nothing to compare against); the ggml-org GGUF repo's own licence tag; whether Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B ships a NOTICE file that Apache-2.0 section 4(d) obliges us to carry; whether the ggml-org Q8_0 main file embeds the MTP tensors or the separate `mtp-*.gguf` (up to 3.2 GB at Q8_0) is needed or ignored by llama-server at b10581; and the expected wall-clock for pulling 47.6 GB through the hub's VPN-limited egress plus the worker-side `-c` cache footprint under ~/.cache/llama.cpp/rpc.

research.dossier:
# R05 — Agent platform matrix (Linux deep; macOS/Windows docs-only; packaging outline)

Date verified: 2026-08-22. Primary sources only: systemd man XML at tag v261.2 (GitHub raw; freedesktop.org was unreachable from the research host, and the founder laptop runs systemd 261.2 so the tag matches the fleet), UPower 1.90.9/1.91.2 docs, kernel ABI/cgroup-v2 docs, KDE/GNOME sources at pinned tags, NVIDIA doc PDFs (MPS r590, MIG r580, nvidia-smi), llama.cpp b10581, Apple open-source man pages at pinned tags + Apple developer-doc JSON, Microsoft Learn, Azure Retail Prices API, uv 0.12.5 / pipx 1.16.7 / PyInstaller 6.22.2 / Briefcase 0.4.4 docs. Several items were additionally exercised read-only on the founder laptop (Arch, systemd 261.2, KDE Plasma on Wayland, RTX 2070 Super) and are flagged "(local test)".

## 1. Linux (full depth)

### 1.1 Running the agent: systemd --user + linger
- The agent should be a **user service** (`~/.config/systemd/user/corvid-agent.service`, `WantedBy=default.target`), not a system service: user units are loaded from `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/systemd/user` (~/.config/systemd/user), `/etc/systemd/user`, `$XDG_DATA_HOME/systemd/user`, `/usr/lib/systemd/user` (R05-F2); `default.target` is "the main target of the user service manager ... a real unit, not an alias" (R05-F3).
- `loginctl enable-linger USER`: "a user manager is spawned for the user at boot and kept around after logouts. This allows users who are not logged in to run long-running services" (R05-F1). Linger is what makes the hub (solarplexus) and any always-on node keep serving after logout. Founder laptop already has Linger=yes (local test).
- Why user-level rather than root: the owner's own manager is "the final authority" (CLAUDE.md §5.3) and `systemctl --user stop corvid-agent` / `systemctl --user kill` is a kill switch that needs no sudo.

### 1.2 Idle detection — the honest picture (Wayland vs X11, GNOME vs KDE)
There is no single Linux idle API. What actually works, per desktop:
- **logind IdleHint** (`loginctl show-session <id> -p IdleHint`, D-Bus `org.freedesktop.login1` Manager/Session `IdleHint`, `IdleSinceHint`): logind only *reflects* what sessions report; `Session.SetIdleHint()` "is called by the session object to update the idle state of the session whenever it changes", and logind.conf warns IdleAction "requires that user sessions correctly report the idle status" (R05-F13). **GNOME does report it** — gnome-session 50.1 calls `SetIdleHint` (R05-F14). **KDE Plasma apparently does not**: a GitHub code search across org:KDE finds no caller, only copies of the interface XML (R05-F15, unverified/negative evidence). ⇒ IdleHint is trustworthy on GNOME, not on Plasma.
- **KDE `org.freedesktop.ScreenSaver.GetSessionIdleTime`** (the seed's suggestion): kscreenlocker v6.7.4 explicitly returns `NotSupported` ("GetSessionIdleTime is not supported on this platform") when the platform is Wayland; it works only on X11 (R05-F16; reproduced on the founder's Plasma-Wayland laptop). `GetActive` (screen locked?) still works on both.
- **GNOME Wayland**: `org.gnome.Mutter.IdleMonitor` at `/org/gnome/Mutter/IdleMonitor/Core` — `GetIdletime()` (ms) and `AddIdleWatch(interval)` → `WatchFired` signal (mutter 50.4, R05-F17). Plain D-Bus, trivial from Python.
- **Compositor-neutral Wayland**: `ext-idle-notify-v1` (wayland-protocols 1.45, MIT): `ext_idle_notifier_v1.get_idle_notification(timeout_ms, seat)` → `idled`/`resumed`; v2 `get_input_idle_notification` ignores idle inhibitors (R05-F18). KWin v6.7.4 implements it; KIdleTime's Wayland plugin consumes it (R05-F19). Mutter: no implementation found (unverified). Needs a real Wayland client (pywayland or a tiny C/Qt helper), not D-Bus.
- **X11**: XScreenSaverQueryInfo `idle` = "milliseconds since the last input was received from the user on any of the input devices"; `xprintidle` (0.3.0, GPL-2.0-only) prints exactly that (R05-F20).
- **Design consequence**: implement idle as a *presence provider chain* with an explicit "unknown" state: Mutter IdleMonitor → ext-idle-notify (KDE/wlroots) → logind IdleHint → XScreenSaver/xprintidle → unknown. When unknown, the agent must fall back to a *load-based* politeness signal (CPU/IO pressure) and say so in the UI; never silently treat unknown as idle.

### 1.3 Battery / AC
- **UPower** (system bus `org.freedesktop.UPower` at `/org/freedesktop/UPower`): `OnBattery` (b) "Indicates whether the system is running on battery power", `LidIsClosed`; per-device `State` (1 Charging, 2 Discharging, 4 Fully charged), `Percentage` (R05-F21). Founder laptop: upower 1.91.3, on-battery=no (local test).
- **sysfs fallback** (no daemon needed): `/sys/class/power_supply/<name>/type` (Mains/Battery), `online` (AC present), `status` ∈ {Unknown, Charging, Discharging, Not charging, Full}, `capacity` 0–100 (R05-F22). Founder laptop: ADP1 type=Mains online=1; BAT1 status=Not charging capacity=94 (local test).
- Cross-platform shortcut: `psutil.sensors_battery()` → (percent, secsleft, power_plugged) (R05-F53) — same call on all three OSes.

### 1.4 Resource caps — cgroup v2 via systemd, with live changes
- `systemd-run --user [--scope] -p CPUQuota=20% -p MemoryMax=2G ... -- cmd` starts a transient unit; `-p` takes "the same format as systemctl's set-property" (R05-F8). `CPUQuota=20%` "ensures that the executed processes will never get more than 20% CPU time on one CPU" (cpu.max); `MemoryHigh=` is "the main control mechanism", `MemoryMax=` "the last line of defense" (OOM-kills inside the unit); `IOWeight=` 1–10000, default 100 (R05-F4–F6). `CPUWeight=idle` exists for "idle scheduling" (R05-F4 note) and systemd.exec offers `Nice=`, `CPUSchedulingPolicy=idle`, `IOSchedulingClass=idle`, `OOMScoreAdjust=` (R05-F27).
- **Live changes**: `systemctl [--user] set-property UNIT CPUQuota=10% MemoryMax=1G` — "The changes are applied immediately, and stored on disk for future boots, unless --runtime is passed" (R05-F7). This is the mechanism for the owner's slider / "pause while I'm gaming" without restarting jobs. Wrap all CORVID work in one slice (e.g. `corvid.slice` under the user manager) so one set-property call re-caps everything.
- **Delegation gotcha (verified)**: systemd's shipped `user@.service` has `Delegate=pids memory cpu` (R05-F9) — **io is not delegated to user managers**. Local test: `systemd-run --user --scope -p CPUQuota=20% -p MemoryMax=100M -p IOWeight=10` produced `cpu.max=20000 100000`, `memory.max=104857600`, but no `io.weight` file (controllers = cpu memory pids) (R05-F10). So CPU/RAM caps work unprivileged out of the box; **disk-I/O caps need a one-time root drop-in** `Delegate=pids memory cpu io` on `user@.service` (R05-F11), or must be done with `IOSchedulingClass=idle` (per-process, no delegation needed).
- Kernel semantics underneath: `cpu.max "$MAX $PERIOD"`, `memory.max` hard limit invoking the OOM killer, `io.weight` [1,10000] default 100 (R05-F12).
- **Kill switch**: `KillMode=control-group` (default) kills "all remaining processes in the control group of this unit" on stop, SIGTERM then SIGKILL after `TimeoutStopSec=`; `systemctl kill --signal=` for instant signalling (R05-F23). Because every job is a transient unit in a CORVID slice, `systemctl --user stop corvid.slice` (or `kill`) is the one-command, no-grace-period kill.

### 1.5 GPU caps — what is real on consumer NVIDIA
- cgroup v2 has **no GPU-compute controller**. Controllers: cpu, memory, io, pids, cpuset, device (BPF), rdma, dmem, hugetlb, misc; the only GPU-adjacent one, `dmem`, "regulates the distribution and accounting of device memory regions" for in-tree DRM drivers (doc example is xe) (R05-F12/F24). Whether the proprietary NVIDIA driver participates is unverified — assume not.
- `nvidia-smi` caps need root: `-pl/--power-limit` ("Requires root", Kepler+, within min/max), `-lgc` lock clocks ("Volta+. Requires root"), `-c/--compute-mode` ("Requires root", resets at reboot) (R05-F25). These are *owner-side* knobs (energy/noise), not per-job shares.
- **MPS** (r590) is aimed at "Hyper-Q capabilities on the latest NVIDIA (Kepler-based) Tesla and Quadro GPUs", Linux-only; Volta+ MPS adds `CUDA_MPS_ACTIVE_THREAD_PERCENTAGE` and `CUDA_MPS_PINNED_DEVICE_MEM_LIMIT` (R05-F26). GeForce support is not stated → open question; do not plan on it.
- **MIG** (r580): Ampere+ with a supported-products table of data-center/RTX PRO parts only — none of the GTX 970 / RTX 2070 Super / RTX 3050 (R05-F27b).
- Therefore GPU "caps" in CORVID are **application-level**: (a) device visibility — `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` or `ggml-rpc-server --device` (R05-F28), or deny `/dev/nvidia*` to a job with systemd `DeviceAllow=`/`DevicePolicy=closed` (R05-F29); (b) VRAM — llama.cpp splits "in proportion to each device's available memory" and `--tensor-split` overrides it; **b10581's rpc-server has no memory-cap flag** (only -t/-d/-H/-p/-c) (R05-F28), so a VRAM ceiling must come from the coordinator's split plan/tensor-split, not the worker; (c) time — the owner's schedule/idle gate simply stops the worker.

## 2. macOS (docs-only)
- **launchd LaunchAgents**: per-user launchd loads `/System/Library/LaunchAgents`, `/Library/LaunchAgents`, and the user's `Library/LaunchAgents`; it "launches any user agents that requested to be running all the time" and sends SIGTERM on logout (R05-F30). Keys (launchd.plist(5), Apple OSS launchd-842.92.1): `KeepAlive`, `RunAtLoad`, `Nice`, `LowPriorityIO`, and `ProcessType` — `Background` jobs get limits "intended to prevent them from disrupting the user experience"; unset ⇒ "light resource limits ... throttling its CPU usage and I/O bandwidth" (R05-F31). That is the free macOS politeness knob; the agent plist should set `ProcessType=Background` (and jobs it spawns inherit via `taskpolicy`).
- Modern registration: `SMAppService` (macOS 13+) registers LaunchAgents/daemons/login items from inside an app bundle (R05-F32) — only relevant if we ever ship a .app; a plain plist in `~/Library/LaunchAgents` is enough for a CLI agent.
- **Idle**: `HIDIdleTime` is the IOHIDSystem registry property `kIOHIDIdleTimeKey = "HIDIdleTime"` published by IOHIDSystem.cpp (IOHIDFamily-2238.120.5) (R05-F33); reading it via `ioreg -c IOHIDSystem` is the conventional path (command form unverified from Apple docs).
- **Battery/AC**: `pmset -g batt` "displays status of batteries and UPSs" (pmset(1), PowerManagement-1846.120.8.0.1); programmatic: IOPowerSources ("uniform access to the state of power sources ... batteries and UPS devices", with change notifications) (R05-F34); or psutil.
- **Caps**: `taskpolicy(8)` (system_cmds-1042.120.1): `-c background|utility|maintenance` QoS clamp, `-b` PRIO_DARWIN_BG, `-d/-g throttle` disk-I/O policy, `-m <MiB>` memory limit, `-p pid` to retarget a running process, `-B` to lift (R05-F35). No cgroup-like hard CPU% on macOS; QoS/background class is the politeness lever.
- **Distribution cost**: notarization is mandatory for Developer-ID software on 10.15+; requires Developer ID cert, Hardened Runtime, secure timestamp, `notarytool` (altool/Xcode≤13 rejected since 2023-11-01) (R05-F36/F37). Apple Developer Program "Enrollment is 99 USD ... per membership year" (R05-F38). Unsigned/unnotarized binaries hit Gatekeeper warnings (R05-F39) — exactly the "unsigned-app warnings scare members" risk in CLAUDE.md §11.

## 3. Windows (docs-only)
- **Idle**: `GetLastInputInfo` "is useful for input idle detection. However, GetLastInputInfo does not provide system-wide user input information across all running sessions ... only the session that invoked the function"; `LASTINPUTINFO.dwTime` is a tick count, "not guaranteed to be incremental" (R05-F40). **Services "cannot directly interact with a user as of Windows Vista"** (Session 0) (R05-F41) ⇒ a Windows service cannot see the user's idle time. Conclusion: run the Windows agent **in the user session** — `schtasks /create /sc ONLOGON ... /it` ("run the scheduled task only when the run as user ... is logged on") or a tray app — not as a service (R05-F42). Task Scheduler's own idle model (Win8+: user absent after 4 min without keyboard/mouse; resource checks every 10 min / 30 s; re-checks on AC/DC and battery events) and `ITaskSettings.StopIfGoingOnBatteries` / `DisallowStartIfOnBatteries` are available for free (R05-F43/F44).
- **Battery/AC**: `GetSystemPowerStatus` → `SYSTEM_POWER_STATUS.ACLineStatus` 0 Offline / 1 Online / 255 Unknown, `BatteryLifePercent`, `SystemStatusFlag` (battery saver) (R05-F45); push notifications via `RegisterPowerSettingNotification` with `GUID_ACDC_POWER_SOURCE` (PoAc/PoDc/PoHot), `GUID_BATTERY_PERCENTAGE_REMAINING`, `GUID_POWER_SAVING_STATUS`, and user-presence GUIDs (`GUID_SESSION_USER_PRESENCE` for user-mode apps; `GUID_GLOBAL_USER_PRESENCE` only for session-0 services, Win8+) (R05-F46).
- **Caps = Job Objects**: CPU hard cap via `JOBOBJECT_CPU_RATE_CONTROL_INFORMATION` (`CpuRate` = percent×100 of 10,000, `JOB_OBJECT_CPU_RATE_CONTROL_HARD_CAP`; Win8+); committed-memory caps via `JOBOBJECT_EXTENDED_LIMIT_INFORMATION.ProcessMemoryLimit/JobMemoryLimit`; `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_AFFINITY`, `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_PRIORITY_CLASS`; `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE`; IO caps (`MaxIops/MaxBandwidth`, Win10+); **kill switch** = `TerminateJobObject` ("Terminates all processes currently associated with the job" incl. nested jobs) (R05-F47–F49). Plus `SetPriorityClass(IDLE_PRIORITY_CLASS | PROCESS_MODE_BACKGROUND_BEGIN)` as the cheap politeness lever (R05-F50).
- **Code signing cost**: Azure Trusted Signing retail price (Azure Retail Prices API, Global): Basic 9.99 USD/month (5,000 signatures/month), Premium 99.99 USD/month, overage 0.005 USD/signature; Public-Trust identities for organizations in listed countries, **individual developers only in US/Canada** (R05-F51/F52). Unsigned or no-reputation binaries: SmartScreen "presents a warning to the user" (R05-F53b). Traditional OV/IV certificates from CAs exist (SSL.com lists IV "no business docs required") but prices were not extractable (unverified).

## 4. Opt-in model — design notes
- Borrow BOINC's vocabulary verbatim (lib/prefs.h): `run_on_batteries`, `run_if_user_active`, `run_gpu_if_user_active`, `suspend_if_no_recent_input` (minutes), `idle_time_to_run`, `cpu_usage_limit` (%), `max_ncpus_pct`, `ram_max_used_busy_frac` / `ram_max_used_idle_frac`, `suspend_cpu_usage`, `start_hour`/`end_hour` (R05-F54). These map 1:1 onto: idle gate (§1.2), battery gate (§1.3), CPUQuota/AllowedCPUs, MemoryHigh/Max, "suspend when host CPU busy", and schedule.
- Every role is a separate opt-in bit: `inference_host`, `batch_jobs`, `gpu_allowed`, `disk_donate_gb`, plus schedule + caps. Default: all off. The agent enforces locally; the coordinator only reads.
- "Unknown presence" (§1.2) must be a first-class state shown in the tray/status page.

## 5. Packaging (outline)
- **Python + uv** (0.12.5): one installer line per OS (`curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh`, PowerShell `irm ... | iex`), `uv python install` fetches Astral python-build-standalone ("Python does not publish official distributable binaries"), `uv tool install corvid-agent` gives an isolated venv with the executable on PATH; `uv self update`; MIT/Apache-2.0 (R05-F55/F56). **pipx** (1.16.7, MIT) is the same idea without Python management (R05-F57). Neither needs code signing; friends see a terminal for 30 s and no unsigned-app dialog for the agent itself (uv's own installer is signed by Astral — out of our hands).
- **PyInstaller** (6.22.2): one-file mode unpacks to a temp `_MEIxxxxxx` folder on every start ("a little slower to start"); `--windowed` makes a .app; `--codesign-identity` enables hardened runtime and "requires ... a valid Apple-issued code signing certificate"; GPL-2.0-with-exception (bundled apps may be closed/any licence) (R05-F58/F59). **Briefcase** (0.4.4, BSD-3) produces .app / MSI / Linux packages and documents the signing-identity chores (R05-F60). Both single-binary routes reintroduce notarization ($99/yr) and Windows signing ($9.99/mo) — the exact "$0 budget" and "installer support burden" costs CLAUDE.md §11 warns about.
- Recommendation below: v1 = uv-based install script + systemd/launchd/Task-Scheduler registration; revisit single binary only in Phase 4 if non-technical onboarding demands it.

## 6. Local verification summary (founder laptop, 2026-08-22)
systemd 261.2, cgroup2fs; KDE Plasma, XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland; Linger=yes; user manager controllers `cpu memory pids` (DelegateControllers); transient scope honoured CPUQuota/MemoryMax, ignored IOWeight; `org.freedesktop.ScreenSaver.GetSessionIdleTime` → "not supported on this platform"; `org.gnome.Mutter.IdleMonitor` absent (expected); upower 1.91.3 on-battery=no; sysfs ADP1 online=1 / BAT1 capacity=94.

facts.statement: loginctl enable-linger USER: "If enabled for a specific user, a user manager is spawned for the user at boot and kept around after logouts. This allows users who are not logged in to run long-running services."

User-mode unit load path (systemd --user) includes $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/systemd/user (~/.config/systemd/user, 'User configuration'), $XDG_CONFIG_DIRS/systemd/user, /etc/systemd/user, $XDG_DATA_HOME/systemd/user, /usr/local/lib/systemd/user and /usr/lib/systemd/user.

For the user service manager, default.target "is the main target of the user service manager, started by default when the service manager is invoked ... it is a real unit, not an alias" (so user services use WantedBy=default.target).

CPUQuota= controls cpu.max on cgroup v2; "Takes a percentage value ... relative to the total CPU time available on one CPU. Use values > 100% for allotting CPU time on more than one CPU." Example in the man page: "CPUQuota=20% ensures that the executed processes will never get more than 20% CPU time on one CPU." CPUWeight= accepts the special value "idle" (cpu.idle) so the cgroup gets CPU only when nothing else wants it.

MemoryMax= is the "absolute limit on memory usage ... If memory usage cannot be contained under the limit, out-of-memory killer is invoked inside the unit. It is recommended to use MemoryHigh= as the main control mechanism and use MemoryMax= as the last line of defense." MemoryHigh= is a throttling limit ("processes are heavily slowed down and memory is taken away aggressively"). Both accept K/M/G/T suffixes or a percentage of installed RAM.

IOWeight= "Takes a single weight value (between 1 and 10000) to set the default block I/O weight. This controls the io.weight control group attribute, which defaults to 100 ... The available I/O bandwidth is split up among all units within one slice relative to their block I/O weight."

systemctl set-property UNIT PROPERTY=VALUE: "Set the specified unit properties at runtime where this is supported ... many resource control settings (primarily those in systemd.resource-control(5)) may. The changes are applied immediately, and stored on disk for future boots, unless --runtime is passed, in which case the settings only apply until the next reboot." Example: systemctl set-property foobar.service CPUWeight=200 MemoryMax=2G IPAccounting=yes; empty assignment resets to default.

systemd-run: --property=/-p "Sets a property on the scope or service unit that is created. This option takes an assignment in the same format as systemctl(1)'s set-property command"; --scope creates a transient .scope (executed by systemd-run itself, synchronous); --user targets the per-user manager (root slice by default, --slice= to choose); man page example: "systemd-run -p IOWeight=10 updatedb" and "systemd-run --scope --user screen".

The shipped user@.service unit template sets "Delegate=pids memory cpu" (plus DelegateSubgroup=init.scope, KillMode=mixed, Slice=user-%i.slice): only the pids, memory and cpu controllers are delegated to per-user service managers by default — io is not.
facts.version: systemd v261.2; identical line present in /usr/lib/systemd/system/user@.service on the founder laptop (systemd 261.2-1-arch)

facts.statement: (local test, founder laptop, systemd 261.2, cgroup2fs, KDE/Wayland) `systemd-run --user --scope -p CPUQuota=20% -p MemoryMax=100M -p IOWeight=10 -- sh -c ...` created app.slice/<unit>.scope with cpu.max="20000 100000" and memory.max=104857600 applied, but no io.weight file existed (cgroup.controllers = "cpu memory pids"; `systemctl show user@1000.service -p DelegateControllers` = "cpu memory pids"). CPU/RAM caps work unprivileged; IOWeight is silently ineffective for --user units unless io is delegated.
facts.version: systemd 261.2 on Arch (founder laptop); kernel cgroup v2

facts.statement: Delegate= "Takes either a boolean argument or a (possibly empty) list of control group controller names. If true, delegation is turned on, and all supported controllers are enabled for the unit"; delegation makes the unit's cgroup subtree the exclusive property of the delegatee (systemd won't touch sub-cgroups). Hence a root-owned drop-in on user@.service (e.g. Delegate=pids memory cpu io) is the documented way to let per-user managers apply io.weight/io.max.
facts.version: systemd v261.2 (see also docs/CGROUP_DELEGATION.md at v261.2)

facts.statement: Kernel cgroup v2: cpu.max is "$MAX $PERIOD" (default "max 100000"); memory.max is the "Memory usage hard limit ... If a cgroup's memory usage reaches this limit and can't be reduced, the OOM killer is invoked in the cgroup"; io.weight range [1,10000], default 100. Controllers documented: cpu, memory, io, pid, cpuset, device (BPF-based, no interface files), rdma, dmem ("regulates the distribution and accounting of device memory regions"; example shows DRM xe vram), hugetlb, misc. There is no GPU-compute controller.

org.freedesktop.login1: Manager.IdleHint "reflects the idle hint state of the system"; IdleSinceHint/IdleSinceHintMonotonic are timestamps of the last change; Session.SetIdleHint(b) "is called by the session object to update the idle state of the session whenever it changes". logind.conf IdleAction= "requires that user sessions correctly report the idle status to the system" — logind does not measure graphical idleness itself.
facts.version: systemd v261.2 (IdleAction text from man/logind.conf.xml at the same tag)

facts.statement: GNOME reports idleness to logind: gnome-session 50.1 gsm-systemd.c calls org.freedesktop.login1.Session "SetIdleHint" with the session's idle boolean ("Updating systemd idle status"). So loginctl IdleHint is meaningful on GNOME sessions.

No KDE Plasma component appears to call logind SetIdleHint: a GitHub code search for SetIdleHint in org:KDE returned only interface-XML copies (plasma-login-manager, systemdgenie), no caller in kwin/powerdevil/kscreenlocker. Treat loginctl IdleHint as unreliable on Plasma until proven otherwise on a real idle Plasma session.
facts.version: KDE org default branches as indexed by GitHub code search on 2026-08-22 (negative evidence)

facts.statement: KDE kscreenlocker's org.freedesktop.ScreenSaver.GetSessionIdleTime() returns a D-Bus NotSupported error ("GetSessionIdleTime is not supported on this platform") when KWindowSystem::isPlatformWayland(); on X11 it returns KIdleTime::instance()->idleTime(). Reproduced on the founder's Plasma-Wayland laptop via busctl (Call failed: GetSessionIdleTime is not supported on this platform). GetActive/GetActiveTime (lock state) remain available.

GNOME/Mutter exposes org.gnome.Mutter.IdleMonitor ("used by gnome-desktop to implement user activity monitoring") with GetIdletime() -> t (idle time), AddIdleWatch(interval ms) -> id firing WatchFired, AddUserActiveWatch, RemoveWatch; object path /org/gnome/Mutter/IdleMonitor/Core. gnome-shell 50.4 also exposes org.gnome.ScreenSaver GetActive/GetActiveTime/ActiveChanged (lock state).

Wayland ext-idle-notify-v1 (staging, wayland-protocols 1.45, MIT, (c) Martin Gräßlin 2015 / Simon Ser 2022): ext_idle_notifier_v1.get_idle_notification(timeout ms, wl_seat) creates an ext_idle_notification_v1 that emits idled after no user activity for the timeout and resumed when activity returns; version 2 adds get_input_idle_notification which "ignores idle inhibitors" and counts only keyboard/mouse input.

KWin implements ext-idle-notify-v1 (src/wayland/idlenotify_v1.cpp implements ext_idle_notifier_v1 incl. get_input_idle_notification) and KIdleTime's Wayland plugin consumes ext_idle_notifier_v1/ext_idle_notification_v1 — so on Plasma Wayland this protocol is the supported idle source. No ext-idle-notify implementation was found in GNOME/mutter (GitHub code search) — unverified negative.

X11: the MIT-SCREEN-SAVER extension's XScreenSaverQueryInfo returns an idle field that "specifies the number of milliseconds since the last input was received from the user on any of the input devices"; xprintidle 0.3.0 is a GPL-2.0-only utility that "queries the X server for the user's idle time and prints it to stdout (in milliseconds)" using Xss (libXss).

UPower D-Bus API: system bus name org.freedesktop.UPower, object /org/freedesktop/UPower; Manager properties OnBattery (b, "Indicates whether the system is running on battery power. This property is provided for convenience."), LidIsClosed, LidIsPresent, DaemonVersion; Device properties include Type, Percentage, State (0 Unknown, 1 Charging, 2 Discharging, 3 Empty, 4 Fully charged, 5 Pending charge, 6 Pending discharge), TimeToEmpty/TimeToFull. Local: upower 1.91.3 on founder laptop reports on-battery: no.
facts.version: UPower docs 1.91.2 (Device.html for State enum); dbus/org.freedesktop.UPower.xml at v1.90.9

facts.statement: sysfs power_supply ABI: /sys/class/power_supply/<name>/status valid values "Unknown", "Charging", "Discharging", "Not charging", "Full"; /capacity = 0-100 percent; /online indicates the supply (e.g. AC adapter) is present/online. Founder laptop (local test): ADP1 type=Mains online=1; BAT1 type=Battery status=Not charging capacity=94.

systemd.kill: KillMode= defaults to control-group — "all remaining processes in the control group of this unit will be killed on unit stop"; processes get KillSignal= (default SIGTERM, followed by SIGCONT), then SIGKILL/FinalKillSignal= after TimeoutStopSec= (unless SendSIGKILL=no). systemctl kill PATTERN sends an arbitrary signal (--signal=, --kill-whom=) to a unit's processes.
facts.version: systemd v261.2 (systemctl kill from man/systemctl.xml at same tag)

facts.statement: Whether the NVIDIA proprietary driver charges VRAM to the cgroup v2 dmem controller is not stated in the kernel doc (which shows DRM xe examples) — assume no cgroup-level VRAM or GPU-time control exists for CORVID's NVIDIA nodes.

nvidia-smi: -pl/--power-limit "Only on supported devices from Kepler family. Value needs to be between Min and Max Power Limit as reported by nvidia-smi. Requires root."; -lgc/--lock-gpu-clocks "Supported on Volta+. Requires root."; -c/--compute-mode "Requires root ... does not persist across reboots" (modes DEFAULT / EXCLUSIVE_PROCESS / PROHIBITED); nvidia-smi supports "Tesla, Quadro, GRID and GeForce devices from Fermi and higher" with "GeForce Titan series devices ... supported for most functions with very limited information provided for the remainder of the Geforce brand".
facts.version: nvidia-smi documentation page as served 2026-08-22 (no release tag on page)

facts.statement: CUDA Multi-Process Service (MPS) doc r590 (Dec 05, 2025): MPS is designed "to utilize Hyper-Q capabilities on the latest NVIDIA (Kepler-based) Tesla and Quadro GPUs"; "MPS is only supported on the Linux and QNX operating systems"; Volta+ MPS supports execution-resource provisioning via CUDA_MPS_ACTIVE_THREAD_PERCENTAGE ("On Volta GPUs, this environment variable sets the portion of the available threads that can be used by the client contexts") and CUDA_MPS_PINNED_DEVICE_MEM_LIMIT ("limits the amount of GPU memory that is allocatable by CUDA APIs by the client process"). GeForce support is not stated.

systemd.exec politeness knobs: Nice= (-20..19), CPUSchedulingPolicy= (other, batch, idle, fifo, rr, ext), IOSchedulingClass= (realtime, best-effort, idle; kernel default best-effort/4), IOSchedulingPriority= (0-7), OOMScoreAdjust= (-1000..1000). These apply per process without cgroup delegation.

NVIDIA MIG User Guide r580: "MIG is supported on GPUs starting with the NVIDIA Ampere generation (that is, GPUs with compute capability >= 8.0)" and the Supported GPU Products table lists data-center/RTX PRO parts (e.g. H100, A100-class, RTX PRO 6000/5000 Blackwell) — no GeForce products; MIG is not an option for GTX 970 / RTX 2070 Super / RTX 3050.

llama.cpp b10581 tools/rpc: ggml-rpc-server options are -t/--threads, -d/--device <dev1,dev2,...>, -H/--host (default 127.0.0.1), -p/--port, -c/--cache — there is no memory-cap flag; it "exposes all available accelerator devices" (CPU if none); device set controlled via CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES or --device; prints "WARNING: Host ... is != '127.0.0.1' Never expose the RPC server to an open network! This is an experimental feature and is not secure!"; llama.cpp "distributes model weights and the KV cache across all available devices ... in proportion to each device's available memory", overridable with --tensor-split. Licence MIT.

systemd DeviceAllow= "Control access to specific device nodes by the executed processes ... implemented using eBPF filtering" (r/w/m per node or char-/block- class); DevicePolicy=strict|closed|auto (auto default allows all devices if no DeviceAllow= is present). Can deny /dev/nvidia* to a batch-job unit.

Apple 'Creating Launch Daemons and Agents': when a user logs in a per-user launchd "loads the parameters for each launch-on-demand user agent from the property list files found in /System/Library/LaunchAgents, /Library/LaunchAgents, and the user's individual Library/LaunchAgents directory ... It launches any user agents that requested to be running all the time ... When the user logs out, it sends a SIGTERM signal to all of the user agents that it started." KeepAlive "specifies whether your daemon launches on-demand or must always be running".
facts.version: Apple Documentation Archive (Daemons and Services Programming Guide)

facts.statement: launchd.plist(5): KeepAlive (default false; true keeps job alive unconditionally or dictionary of conditions), RunAtLoad (default false), Nice <integer> (nice value applied to the daemon), LowPriorityIO <boolean> (kernel treats daemon's file-system I/O as low priority), ProcessType <string>: "If left unspecified, the system will apply light resource limits to the job, throttling its CPU usage and I/O bandwidth"; Background = "processes that do work that was not directly requested by the user. The resource limits applied to Background jobs are intended to prevent them from disrupting the user experience"; Standard/Adaptive/Interactive also defined.
facts.version: Apple open-source launchd-842.92.1 man page (last open-source launchd; keys still documented in current man launchd.plist — verify on a macOS 14/15 box)

facts.statement: SMAppService (ServiceManagement, macOS 13.0+): "In macOS 13 and later, use SMAppService to register and control LaunchAgents, LaunchDaemons and login items as helper executables for your app" — a replacement for installing property lists in LaunchAgents/LaunchDaemons directories.

IOHIDFamily defines kIOHIDIdleTimeKey as the string "HIDIdleTime" (IOHIDParameter.h) and IOHIDSystem.cpp publishes it with setProperty(kIOHIDIdleTimeKey, idleTimeSerializer) — i.e. the system-wide HID idle time is an IORegistry property of IOHIDSystem (nanoseconds since last HID input). Reading it via `ioreg -c IOHIDSystem | grep HIDIdleTime` is the conventional CLI path but the command form itself is not documented by Apple.
facts.version: IOHIDFamily-2238.120.5 (key definition and setProperty verified; ioreg usage and unit = unverified)

facts.statement: pmset(1): `pmset -g ps` / `pmset -g batt` "displays status of batteries and UPSs"; `-g pslog` gives an ongoing power-source log; -b/-c/-u select battery/charger/UPS settings. IOPowerSources.h: "provides uniform access to the state of power sources attached to the system. You can receive a change notification when any power source data changes. 'Power sources' currently include batteries and UPS devices."
facts.version: PowerManagement-1846.120.8.0.1 man page; IOPowerSources overview from https://developer.apple.com/documentation/iokit/iopowersources_h

facts.statement: taskpolicy(8): "execute a program with an altered I/O or scheduling policy or change settings of already running process" using setiopolicy_np(3) and setpriority(2); -c clamp ("utility", "background", or "maintenance" QoS clamp), -b (PRIO_DARWIN_BG) / -B (move out of background), -d/-g policy (disk I/O policy e.g. throttle), -m limit (memory limit in MiB), -j jetsam priority, -p pid (change a running process); "All children of the specified program also inherit these policies."

Apple notarization: "Beginning in macOS 10.15, all software built after June 1, 2019, and distributed with Developer ID must be notarized"; the notary service requires code signing with a Developer ID certificate, the Hardened Runtime capability, a secure timestamp, no get-task-allow entitlement, linking against the 10.9+ SDK; "Starting November 1, 2023, the Apple notary service no longer accepts uploads from altool or Xcode 13 or earlier" (use notarytool / Xcode 14+). Notarization is automated scanning, not App Review; tickets can be stapled.
facts.version: Apple developer docs as of 2026-08-22 (Markdown/JSON variants of the page)

facts.statement: Hardened Runtime: "To upload a macOS app to be notarized, you must enable the Hardened Runtime capability"; it "does disallow certain less common capabilities, like just-in-time (JIT) compilation" unless an exception entitlement is added — relevant for Python interpreters/PyInstaller bundles.

Apple Developer Program: "Enrollment is 99 USD (or in local currency where available) per membership year" (fee waivers only for nonprofits/educational/government); the free Apple Account tier allows Xcode and on-device testing but not distribution.
facts.version: Apple 'Choosing a Membership' page as of 2026-08-22 (programs page also says '$99 annual membership')

facts.statement: Gatekeeper: "When a user downloads and opens an app ... from outside the App Store, Gatekeeper verifies that the software is from an identified developer, is notarized by Apple to be free of known malicious content, and hasn't been altered" and "requests user approval before opening downloaded software for the first time" — unsigned/un-notarized downloads produce the warning flow CLAUDE.md §11 wants to avoid.
facts.version: Apple Platform Security guide as of 2026-08-22

facts.statement: GetLastInputInfo (winuser.h): "This function is useful for input idle detection. However, GetLastInputInfo does not provide system-wide user input information across all running sessions. Rather, GetLastInputInfo provides session-specific user input information for only the session that invoked the function." LASTINPUTINFO.dwTime is "The tick count when the last input event was received" and "is not guaranteed to be incremental". Min client Windows 2000.

Windows services: "Services cannot directly interact with a user as of Windows Vista" (Session 0 isolation); suggested workarounds are WTSSendMessage or CreateProcessAsUser into the user's session. Services "can execute even when no user is logged on"; sc.exe create supports start= boot|system|auto|demand|disabled|delayed-auto and obj= account.

schtasks /create: /sc ONLOGON "runs whenever a user (any user) logs on"; /sc ONIDLE with /i <idletime> runs when the system is idle; /it "Specifies to run the scheduled task only when the run as user ... is logged on to the computer" (interactive-only); /ru and /rl set run-as user and run level.

Task Scheduler idle conditions: in Windows 8+ "Task Scheduler relies on the operating system power subsystem to detect user presence. By default, the user is considered absent after four minutes of no keyboard or mouse input"; resource checks every 10 minutes when present, 30 seconds when away, plus re-checks on 'User presence state changed', 'AC/DC power source changed', 'Battery level changed'; Windows 7 used 15-minute checks with >90% idle CPU/disk.

ITaskSettings.StopIfGoingOnBatteries: "Gets or sets a Boolean value that indicates that the task will be stopped if the computer is going onto batteries" (XML element StopIfGoingOnBatteries); companion DisallowStartIfOnBatteries property exists — battery politeness is built into Task Scheduler.

GetSystemPowerStatus "indicates whether the system is running on AC or DC power, whether the battery is currently charging, how much battery life remains, and if battery saver is on or off"; SYSTEM_POWER_STATUS.ACLineStatus: 0 Offline, 1 Online, 255 Unknown; BatteryFlag bits (1 high >66%, 2 low <33%, 4 critical...), BatteryLifePercent 0-100/255, SystemStatusFlag (battery saver).

Power setting GUIDs (RegisterPowerSettingNotification): GUID_ACDC_POWER_SOURCE (Data = PoAc 0 / PoDc 1 / PoHot 2), GUID_BATTERY_PERCENTAGE_REMAINING (0-100), GUID_POWER_SAVING_STATUS (battery saver on/off), GUID_IDLE_BACKGROUND_TASK (system busy/good time for background work), GUID_SESSION_USER_PRESENCE for user-mode apps vs GUID_GLOBAL_USER_PRESENCE which "is sent only services and other programs running in session 0" (Windows 8+).

JOBOBJECT_CPU_RATE_CONTROL_INFORMATION (Windows 8+/Server 2012+): with JOB_OBJECT_CPU_RATE_CONTROL_ENABLE | JOB_OBJECT_CPU_RATE_CONTROL_HARD_CAP, CpuRate "Specifies the portion of processor cycles that the threads in a job object can use during each scheduling interval, as the number of cycles per 10,000 cycles ... to let the job use 20% of the CPU, set CpuRate to 20 times 100, or 2,000"; weight-based and min/max-rate modes also exist.

JOBOBJECT_EXTENDED_LIMIT_INFORMATION: ProcessMemoryLimit (with JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_PROCESS_MEMORY) "specifies the limit for the virtual memory that can be committed by a process"; JobMemoryLimit (JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_JOB_MEMORY) for the whole job; basic limit flags include JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_AFFINITY, JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_PRIORITY_CLASS, JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_SCHEDULING_CLASS and JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE ("all processes associated with the job terminate when the last handle to the job is closed"). JOBOBJECT_IO_RATE_CONTROL_INFORMATION (Windows 10+) caps MaxIops/MaxBandwidth per volume.
facts.version: Microsoft Learn as of 2026-08-22 (basic limits: ns-winnt-jobobject_basic_limit_information; IO: jobapi2 jobobject_io_rate_control_information)

facts.statement: TerminateJobObject "Terminates all processes currently associated with the job. If the job is nested, this function terminates all processes currently associated with the job and all of its child jobs in the hierarchy" (handle needs JOB_OBJECT_TERMINATE; Windows XP+). Job objects "allow groups of processes to be managed as a unit" — the Windows kill switch / cgroup analogue.

SetPriorityClass: IDLE_PRIORITY_CLASS ("threads ... run only when the system is idle"), BELOW_NORMAL_PRIORITY_CLASS, and PROCESS_MODE_BACKGROUND_BEGIN ("The system lowers the resource scheduling priorities of the process (and its threads) so that it can perform background work without significantly affecting activity in the foreground"; current process only).

Azure Trusted Signing (Artifact Signing) retail prices, region Global, effective 2024-06-01: Basic Account 9.99 USD per month, Premium Account 99.99 USD per month, Signature Overage 0.005 USD per signature (Basic/Premium included signatures billed at 0); pricing page quotas: Basic 5,000 signatures/month, Premium 100,000.

facts.statement: Trusted Signing eligibility: "Public Trust certificates are available to organizations in the United States, Canada, the European Union, the United Kingdom, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, South Korea, Singapore, Switzerland, Norway, and Israel. Individual developers must be located in the United States or Canada. These geographic restrictions do not apply to Private Trust certificates." Identity validation can only be completed in the Azure portal.
psutil.sensors_battery() returns sbattery(percent, secsleft, power_plugged) — a single cross-platform battery/AC call (Linux, Windows, macOS); psutil is BSD-3-Clause.
facts.version: psutil v7.2.2 (docs 'latest'; LICENSE at tag v7.2.2)

facts.statement: Microsoft Defender SmartScreen "provides reputation checks for apps, checking downloaded programs and the digital signature used to sign a file. If a URL, a file, an app, or a certificate has an established reputation, users don't see any warnings. If there's no reputation, the item is marked as a higher risk and presents a warning to the user."

BOINC global preferences (lib/prefs.h) define the reference opt-in/politeness vocabulary: run_on_batteries, run_if_user_active, run_gpu_if_user_active, suspend_if_no_recent_input, idle_time_to_run, cpu_usage_limit, max_ncpus_pct, niu_* (not-in-use variants), ram_max_used_busy_frac / ram_max_used_idle_frac, suspend_cpu_usage, start_hour/end_hour; the PrefsImpl wiki shows the same as <global_preferences> XML (run_on_batteries, run_if_user_active, suspend_if_no_recent_input, idle_time_to_run, cpu_usage_limit, ...).

uv 0.12.5: "A single tool to replace pip, pip-tools, pipx, poetry, pyenv, twine, virtualenv, and more"; "Installs and manages Python versions"; "Runs and installs tools published as Python packages"; "Supports macOS, Linux, and Windows"; standalone installer `curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh` (version-pinned URLs available) and PowerShell `irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex`; `uv self update` when installed via the standalone installer. Licensed MIT (LICENSE-MIT, Astral Software Inc.) or Apache-2.0.

uv Python management: `uv python install` — "Python does not publish official distributable binaries. As such, uv uses distributions from the Astral python-build-standalone project"; uv auto-downloads required Python versions. `uv tool install <pkg>`: "When a tool is installed, its executables are placed in a bin directory in the PATH which allows the tool to be run without uv" in "an isolated virtual environment"; `uvx` runs tools in temporary isolated environments.

pipx "installs and runs end-user Python applications in isolated environments ... creates a separate virtual environment for each application, so their dependencies never collide and an uninstall leaves nothing behind"; licence MIT (Chad Smith and contributors).

PyInstaller 6.22.2: one-file mode — the bootloader "creates a temporary folder ... named _MEIxxxxxx" and "uncompresses the support files and writes copies into the temporary folder. This can take a little time. That is why a one-file app is a little slower to start"; one-folder is the default and "much easier to diagnose"; -F/--onefile, -D/--onedir, -w/--windowed ("On macOS this also triggers building a macOS .app bundle"), --osx-bundle-identifier, --target-architecture x86_64|arm64|universal2; --codesign-identity (ad-hoc signing otherwise) — "When codesign identity is specified, PyInstaller also turns on hardened runtime ... This requires the codesign identity to be a valid Apple-issued code signing certificate, and will not work with self-signed certificates."
facts.version: PyInstaller 6.22.2 (usage.html, feature-notes.html on the same docs site)

facts.statement: PyInstaller licence: "distributed under a dual-licensing scheme using both the GPL 2.0 License, with an exception that allows you to use it to build commercial products ... and the Apache License, version 2.0, which only applies to a certain few files"; "You may use PyInstaller to bundle commercial applications out of your source code" — bundled CORVID binaries would not become GPL.

Briefcase "is a tool for converting a Python project into a standalone native application. It supports producing binaries for: macOS, as a standalone .app; Windows, as an MSI installer; Linux, as a native system package; iOS ...; Android ...; the Web"; docs include 'Obtaining a Code Signing identity' for macOS/Windows/Android. Licence BSD-3-Clause (Russell Keith-Magee).

Python is licensed under the Python Software Foundation License Version 2 (GPL-compatible, permits redistribution of modified versions without source); astral-sh/python-build-standalone's own LICENSE is MPL-2.0 (the shipped interpreters remain PSF-licensed plus bundled third-party licences).
facts.version: docs.python.org/3 as of 2026-08-22; python-build-standalone LICENSE on main 2026-08-22

facts.statement: PyInstaller is not a cross-compiler: a Windows build must be made on Windows, a macOS build on macOS, a Linux build on Linux (three build machines or CI runners per release).
facts.version: PyInstaller 6.22.2 — requirements page lists per-OS requirements but the explicit 'no cross-compilation' sentence was not captured

facts.statement: Vendor OV/IV Windows code-signing certificates: SSL.com's product page lists IV Code Signing ("For individual developers ... No business docs required"), OV ("Organization name verified"), and EV; prices are rendered client-side and could not be extracted — assume order-of-magnitude hundreds of USD/year until checked on the vendor page.

recommendations: Linux agent = a per-user systemd service (~/.config/systemd/user/corvid-agent.service, WantedBy=default.target) plus `loginctl enable-linger` on always-on nodes (hub, optiplex); never a root service. Kill switch = `systemctl --user stop corvid.slice` (all CORVID work lives in one user slice) — KillMode=control-group guarantees nothing survives.

Run every job as a transient unit: `systemd-run --user --slice=corvid.slice -p CPUQuota=<n>% -p MemoryHigh=<x> -p MemoryMax=<y> -p CPUWeight=idle -p IOSchedulingClass=idle -p Nice=19 ...`; implement the owner's live slider as `systemctl --user set-property corvid.slice CPUQuota=... MemoryMax=...` (applied immediately, persisted unless --runtime).

Document the io-delegation gotcha in the Linux install guide: CPU/RAM caps work unprivileged; IOWeight/IOReadBandwidthMax need a one-time sudo drop-in `/etc/systemd/system/user@.service.d/corvid.conf` with `[Service]\nDelegate=pids memory cpu io` (spike this on the hub; until then rely on IOSchedulingClass=idle).

Build idle detection as a provider chain with an explicit UNKNOWN state: (1) org.gnome.Mutter.IdleMonitor.GetIdletime (GNOME, D-Bus), (2) ext-idle-notify-v1 client (KDE/wlroots Wayland — small helper; spike pywayland vs a 50-line C/Qt binary), (3) logind IdleHint (trust only when provider 1 is present/GNOME), (4) XScreenSaver/xprintidle (X11), (5) UNKNOWN → use load/pressure heuristics and show 'presence unknown' in the status page. Do not use org.freedesktop.ScreenSaver.GetSessionIdleTime (NotSupported on Plasma Wayland).

Battery/AC: use psutil.sensors_battery() as the one cross-platform call; on Linux fall back to /sys/class/power_supply/*/online + status when psutil is unavailable; default policy run_on_batteries=false, and on AC-loss pause immediately (don't wait for the next heartbeat).

GPU policy for the spec: treat GPU as all-or-nothing per job/time-window — no compute shares on GeForce (no MIG; MPS is Tesla/Quadro-targeted and Linux-only; cgroup v2 has no GPU controller). Implement 'GPU off' via DeviceAllow/DevicePolicy=closed or CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' on the job unit, and VRAM ceilings via the coordinator's --tensor-split plan (ggml-rpc-server b10581 has no --mem flag). Owner-side nvidia-smi -pl power caps are root-only — document as optional sudo step, never required.

macOS agent = LaunchAgent plist in ~/Library/LaunchAgents with KeepAlive=true, RunAtLoad=true, ProcessType=Background, LowPriorityIO=true, Nice=10+; spawn jobs via `taskpolicy -c background` (and -m MiB for a memory limit); idle via IOHIDSystem HIDIdleTime (ioreg) + org.freedesktop.ScreenSaver-equivalent lock check; battery via pmset -g batt/psutil. Defer SMAppService/.app bundle until a tray UI exists.

Windows agent = per-user Scheduled Task (ONLOGON, /it, highest-available run level not required) running the Python agent in the user session — NOT a Windows service — because GetLastInputInfo is session-scoped and services live in Session 0. Use Job Objects for each job (CPU hard cap via CpuRate, JobMemoryLimit, KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE, TerminateJobObject as kill switch) and register GUID_ACDC_POWER_SOURCE / GUID_SESSION_USER_PRESENCE notifications; also set Task Scheduler StopIfGoingOnBatteries for belt-and-braces.

Packaging v1 (Phases 2–3): Python 3.12+ app published as a wheel, installed with `uv tool install corvid-agent` (uv manages Python via python-build-standalone); one install script per OS that also registers the systemd/launchd/Task-Scheduler unit; `uv tool upgrade` for updates. This keeps the $0 budget (no Apple $99/yr, no Trusted Signing $9.99/mo) and avoids Gatekeeper/SmartScreen dialogs for our own code. Revisit PyInstaller/Briefcase single binaries in Phase 4 only if non-technical onboarding fails; budget $99/yr (Apple) + $9.99/mo (Azure Trusted Signing, individual identity requires US/Canada) if that day comes, and note PyInstaller needs per-OS build machines.

Opt-in schema (coordinator DB + agent config): boolean roles {inference_host, batch_jobs, gpu_allowed, disk_donate}, caps {cpu_quota_pct, allowed_cpus, mem_high, mem_max, io_weight|io_idle, vram_cap_mb (coordinator-enforced)}, politeness {run_if_user_active=false, idle_minutes, run_on_batteries=false, suspend_cpu_usage_pct, schedule windows} — borrow BOINC's names so the semantics are already documented; the agent enforces locally and reports the effective policy in its heartbeat.
Add ADR: 'Idle/presence detection is best-effort and desktop-specific; UNKNOWN presence never counts as idle' and 'GPU sharing is temporal, not spatial, on consumer NVIDIA'.
open_questions: Does KDE Plasma (powerdevil/kwin 6.x) ever call logind SetIdleHint? Negative code-search evidence only — confirm by leaving a Plasma Wayland session idle past the power-saving timeout and watching `loginctl show-session -p IdleHint`.
Does GNOME Mutter (50.x) implement ext-idle-notify-v1? Code search found nothing; if not, the provider chain must keep the Mutter D-Bus path as a separate branch (it does today).

Which Wayland client route for ext-idle-notify-v1 from a Python agent: pywayland (pure Python, needs scanner-generated bindings) vs a tiny C/Qt helper binary vs depending on a distro-packaged tool (e.g. swayidle)? Spike on the founder's Plasma laptop.

Does CUDA MPS actually start on GeForce (Turing/Ampere) with driver 535/CUDA 12.2 (hub GTX 970, Maxwell) and CUDA 13.1 (RTX 3050)? The doc scopes MPS to Tesla/Quadro; a 10-minute spike (nvidia-cuda-mps-control -d, then a CUDA client) settles whether active-thread-percentage caps are even an option.
Does the NVIDIA proprietary driver integrate with the cgroup v2 dmem controller (kernel 6.14+)? If yes, VRAM caps per job become possible on Linux; if no (expected), VRAM stays coordinator-planned.

Does the older llama.cpp rpc-server still used on the hub (driver 535/CUDA 12.2 may force an older build) have the removed -m/--mem flag? Pin the exact llama.cpp tag per node and check `ggml-rpc-server --help`.

On the hub with Tailscale in userspace mode, is there a tailscale0 interface to bind ggml-rpc-server/agent listeners to at all? (Out of R05 scope but gates the 'bind to tailnet interface only' rule on that node.)

macOS: confirm on a real Mac (macOS 14/15) that `man launchd.plist` still documents ProcessType/LowPriorityIO as in the 2013 open-source man page, and that `ioreg -c IOHIDSystem` reports HIDIdleTime in nanoseconds under current SIP settings.

Windows: is a per-user scheduled task at logon acceptable to members vs a tray app with autostart? Both avoid Session 0; the tray app gives the visible kill switch CLAUDE.md §5.4 requires — decide in Phase 4 UI work.
Will any friend's machine run X11 still (older Linux) — i.e. is xprintidle worth shipping as an optional dependency, or is XScreenSaver via ctypes enough?

Azure Trusted Signing individual identity requires US/Canada residency and an Azure billing account; is the founder eligible, and is the $9.99/mo acceptable as a Phase-4 line item if a single-binary Windows agent is ever shipped?
Exact current prices of IV/OV code-signing certificates from CAs (SSL.com/DigiCert pages are JS-rendered) — only needed if Trusted Signing is ruled out.

verdicts.reason: Fetched https://raw.githubusercontent.com/systemd/systemd/v261.2/man/loginctl.xml (HTTP 200; tag v261.2 confirmed via GitHub API). Lines 189-195 of the enable-linger/disable-linger entry read verbatim: "Enable/disable user lingering for one or more users. If enabled for a specific user, a user manager is spawned for the user at boot and kept around after logouts. This allows users who are not logged in to run long-running services. Takes one or more user names or numeric UIDs as argument. If no argument is specified, enables/disables lingering for the user of the session of the caller." (feature marked "Added in version 233"). The freedesktop.org 'latest' HTML page (which reports itself as systemd 261.2) contains the identical sentence. The source is the upstream systemd manual (primary), the version matches, and the quotation is exact. Only nit: the claim's synopsis shows "USER" as mandatory whereas the man page shows it as optional ([USER...]) — immaterial to the quoted text.

Fetched the cited primary source (systemd/systemd tag v261.2, man/systemd.unit.xml; tag verified via GitHub API, HTTP 200). The "Unit File Load Path" section's table "Load path when running in user mode (--user)" lists, among other entries, exactly the six paths in the claim: "$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/systemd/user or $HOME/.config/systemd/user" with description "User configuration ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME is used if set, ~/.config otherwise)"; "$XDG_CONFIG_DIRS/systemd/user or /etc/xdg/systemd/user"; "/etc/systemd/user" (User units created by the administrator); "$XDG_DATA_HOME/systemd/user or $HOME/.local/share/systemd/user"; "/usr/local/lib/systemd/user" (User units installed by the administrator); and "/usr/lib/systemd/user" (User units installed by the distribution package manager). The claim says the load path "includes" these (not that it is exhaustive), and their relative order in the claim matches the table's priority order. The source is primary (systemd's own man page source at the stated version) and current for v261.2. Minor non-refuting note: the table also contains runtime/transient/generator/XDG_DATA_DIRS entries not mentioned in the claim, and $XDG_CONFIG_DIRS defaults to /etc/xdg when unset.

Fetched https://raw.githubusercontent.com/systemd/systemd/v261.2/man/systemd.special.xml (HTTP 200; tag v261.2 confirmed to exist via the GitHub refs API). Under "Units managed by the user service manager" / "Special User Units", the default.target entry reads verbatim: "This is the main target of the user service manager, started by default when the service manager is invoked. Various services that compose the normal user session should be pulled into this target. In this regard, default.target is similar to multi-user.target in the system instance, but it is a real unit, not an alias." (version-info marker v242). The quoted fragments in the claim match exactly; the ellipsis elides only the middle sentence. The parenthetical "(so user services use WantedBy=default.target)" is an inference, not a literal sentence in the page, but it follows directly from "services ... should be pulled into this target" (the [Install] mechanism for pulling a unit into a target is WantedBy=/RequiredBy=), and the page's separate warning against WantedBy=default.target applies only to the system instance's default.target alias, not the user instance's real unit. Source is primary (upstream systemd man page XML at the pinned tag) and current for v261.2. Not refuted.

Fetched the cited primary source (raw man/systemd.resource-control.xml at tag v261.2, 110 KB, valid DocBook). It supports every part of the claim verbatim or near-verbatim. CPUQuota= (lines 232-252): "Takes a percentage value, suffixed with "%". The percentage specifies how much CPU time the unit shall get at maximum, relative to the total CPU time available on one CPU. Use values > 100% for allotting CPU time on more than one CPU. This controls the cpu.max attribute on the unified control group hierarchy and cpu.cfs_quota_us on legacy." The example is exact: "Example: CPUQuota=20% ensures that the executed processes will never get more than 20% CPU time on one CPU." CPUWeight= (lines 187-213): "These options accept an integer value or the special string "idle"" ... "If set to the special string "idle", mark the cgroup for "idle scheduling", which means that it will get CPU resources only when there are no processes not marked in this way to execute in this cgroup or its siblings. This setting corresponds to the cpu.idle cgroup attribute." Minor precision note only (not a refutation): the man page scopes idle scheduling to "this cgroup or its siblings" and adds that on cgroup-v1 "idle" is equivalent to the minimum weight; the claim's "gets CPU only when nothing else wants it" is a fair paraphrase of the v2 behaviour. Source is primary (systemd's own repo at the stated version tag).

Fetched the cited primary source (systemd repo, tag v261.2, man/systemd.resource-control.xml; HTTP 200, 110159 bytes). The MemoryMax= entry (lines 402-405) reads verbatim: "Specify the absolute limit on memory usage of the executed processes in this unit. If memory usage cannot be contained under the limit, out-of-memory killer is invoked inside the unit. It is recommended to use MemoryHigh= as the main control mechanism and use MemoryMax= as the last line of defense." The MemoryHigh= entry (lines 372-374) reads: "Specify the throttling limit on memory usage ... the processes are heavily slowed down and memory is taken away aggressively in such cases." Both entries (lines 376-379 and 407-409) state the value may be suffixed with K, M, G or T (base 1024) or given as a percentage "relative to the installed physical memory on the system". Every quoted fragment and paraphrase in the claim matches the v261.2 source exactly; the source is the upstream man-page source at the stated version, i.e. primary. No refutation found.

Fetched https://raw.githubusercontent.com/systemd/systemd/v261.2/man/systemd.resource-control.xml (HTTP 200, 110159 bytes). The IOWeight=/StartupIOWeight= entry (lines 618-640) reads verbatim: "Takes a single weight value (between 1 and 10000) to set the default block I/O weight. This controls the <literal>io.weight</literal> control group attribute, which defaults to 100. For details about this control group attribute, see IO Interface Files. The available I/O bandwidth is split up among all units within one slice relative to their block I/O weight. A higher weight means more I/O bandwidth, a lower weight means less." The claim's quoted text matches the source exactly (the ellipsis elides only the "For details..." sentence). The source is primary (systemd's own man page source at the v261.2 tag) and current for the stated version; the setting is marked as added in v230 and applies to the unified (cgroup v2) hierarchy io controller.

Fetched https://raw.githubusercontent.com/systemd/systemd/v261.2/man/systemctl.xml (HTTP 200; tag v261.2 confirmed via GitHub API, sha d5e8f63a). The set-property varlistentry (lines 674-707) contains the quoted sentences verbatim: "Set the specified unit properties at runtime where this is supported... Not all properties may be changed at runtime, but many resource control settings (primarily those in systemd.resource-control(5)) may. The changes are applied immediately, and stored on disk for future boots, unless --runtime is passed, in which case the settings only apply until the next reboot." Both examples appear verbatim: "systemctl set-property foobar.service CPUWeight=200 MemoryMax=2G IPAccounting=yes" and "systemctl set-property avahi-daemon.service IPAddressDeny=". Cross-checked https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html (renders "systemd 261.2"); identical wording. Source is primary (systemd's own manpage source at the stated tag). One minor paraphrase nuance, not a refutation: the source says an empty assignment "usually resets a property to its defaults" (hedged with "usually"), whereas the claim's summary says "empty assignment resets to default". Also note the --runtime option text (line 2678ff) separately confirms runtime changes go to /run/ rather than /etc/ and are lost on reboot.
verdicts.corrected_statement: No correction needed; optionally tighten the paraphrase to "assigning an empty setting usually resets a property to its defaults" to match the source's hedge.

verdicts.reason: Fetched the cited primary source (raw man/systemd-run.xml at tag v261.2; GitHub tag v261.2 confirmed to exist; freedesktop 'latest' page also reports systemd 261.2). Every element of the claim checks out verbatim: (1) --property=/-p text (lines 137-143): "Sets a property on the scope or service unit that is created. This option takes an assignment in the same format as systemctl(1)'s set-property command." (2) --scope (line 115-119): "Create a transient .scope unit instead of the default transient .service unit"; Description (lines 75-81): a scope-mode command "will be executed by systemd-run itself as parent process ... Execution in this case is synchronous, and will return only when the command finishes." (3) --user is xi:included from user-system-options.xml at v261.2: "Talk to the service manager of the calling user, rather than the service manager of the system"; --slice= (lines 161-166): "instead of system.slice (when running in --system mode) or the root slice (when running in --user mode)." (4) Examples present: line 661 "# systemd-run -p IOWeight=10 updatedb" and line 702 "$ systemd-run --scope --user screen". The freedesktop latest page contains the same strings. Source is primary (upstream systemd repository) and current for the stated version. Claim stands.

Fetched the cited primary source (raw units/user@.service.in at tag v261.2, HTTP 200). Its [Service] section contains exactly: Slice=user-%i.slice, KillMode=mixed, Delegate=pids memory cpu, DelegateSubgroup=init.scope (plus User=%i, PAMName=systemd-user, Type=notify-reload, ExecStart={{LIBEXECDIR}}/systemd --user, TasksMax=infinity, etc.). 'io' is absent from the Delegate= list. Cross-checked /usr/lib/systemd/system/user@.service on this machine (systemd 261 (261.2-1-arch), pacman systemd 261.2-1): byte-identical [Service] directives incl. 'Delegate=pids memory cpu'. Local systemd.resource-control(5) confirms that a Delegate= controller list enables only the named controllers for the unit, with the caveat that 'additional controllers other than the ones specified might be made available as well, depending on configuration of the containing slice unit' — the claim's 'by default' wording is consistent with that caveat. Source is primary (upstream repo at the stated tag) and current for the stated version. Claim stands as written.

Cited source is primary and current for the stated version: units/user@.service.in at tag v261.2 (HTTP 200) sets `Delegate=pids memory cpu` (plus DelegateSubgroup=init.scope) — io is not delegated, so the user manager cannot apply IOWeight, consistent with the observed DelegateControllers="cpu memory pids" and absent io.weight file. Cross-checked src/core/cgroup.c at v261.2: unit_get_target_mask() masks out controllers not in manager->cgroup_supported with no warning (only BPF firewall warns; supported-controller list logged at debug only), confirming "silently ineffective". src/core/unit.c unit_set_default_slice() places user-manager units in app.slice; cgroup-util.h enum order yields "cpu memory pids"; CPUQuota=20% -> cpu.max "20000 100000" and MemoryMax=100M -> 104857600 are standard encodings. Arch's systemd 261.2 PKGBUILD applies only a device-access-groups patch, not touching user@.service.

Fetched the cited primary source (raw man/systemd.resource-control.xml at tag v261.2, HTTP 200). The quoted sentence appears verbatim in the Delegate= entry: "Takes either a boolean argument or a (possibly empty) list of control group controller names. If true, delegation is turned on, and all supported controllers are enabled for the unit, making them available to the unit's processes for management. ... If set to a list of controllers, delegation is turned on, and the specified controllers are enabled for the unit." The ownership claim is also supported there ("the service manager will refrain from manipulating control groups or moving processes below the unit's control group ... the control group tree below the unit's control group is owned and managed by the unit itself") and by docs/CGROUP_DELEGATION.md at v261.2 ("those then become exclusive property of your program, systemd won't touch them"). The user@.service inference holds for this version: (a) the same man page says that when the delegatee is systemd in user@.service it "will repeat the same logic as the system instance and enable controllers for user units which have resource limits configured"; (b) units/user@.service.in at v261.2 ships Delegate=pids memory cpu (no io), so io must be added for per-user IOWeight=/IOReadBandwidthMax= (io.weight/io.max) to take effect; (c) src/core/load-fragment.c config_parse_delegate at v261.2 ORs list-form controllers into the existing mask, so a drop-in line Delegate=pids memory cpu io (or just Delegate=io) is additive; (d) user@.service(5) at v261.2 documents drop-ins as the standard way to adjust these units. Minor caveat only: no single upstream sentence literally says "add io to user@.service's Delegate= for per-user io.weight"; the claim is a sound composition of documented statements, and the supported controller list (man/supported-controllers.xml) includes io. Not refuted.

Fetched https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/latest/admin-guide/cgroup-v2.html on 2026-08-22 (primary source: kernel.org official admin-guide, author Tejun Heo). Every element of the claim matches verbatim: cpu.max — "The default is 'max 100000'. ... It's in the following format: $MAX $PERIOD"; memory.max — "Memory usage hard limit. This is the main mechanism to limit memory usage of a cgroup. If a cgroup's memory usage reaches this limit and can't be reduced, the OOM killer is invoked in the cgroup." (the claim's ellipsis correctly elides only the middle sentence); io.weight — "The default is 'default 100'" and "The weights are in the range [1, 10000]"; the Controllers chapter's section headings are exactly CPU, Memory, IO, PID, Cpuset, Device controller, RDMA, DMEM, HugeTLB, Misc; Device controller — "has no interface files and is implemented on top of cgroup BPF"; DMEM — "The 'dmem' controller regulates the distribution and accounting of device memory regions" with examples "An example for xe follows: drm/0000:03:00.0/vram0 ..."; and the document contains no occurrence of "gpu" or any GPU-compute controller (the only GPU-related content is the dmem/xe vram example). Claim is supported as stated for the 'latest' docs on the stated date.

Fetched both cited primary sources at tag v261.2 (HTTP 200). man/org.freedesktop.login1.xml line 821: "The IdleHint property reflects the idle hint state of the system"; lines 824-826: IdleSinceHint/IdleSinceHintMonotonic "encode the timestamps of the last change of the idle hint boolean" (CLOCK_REALTIME/CLOCK_MONOTONIC, usec); lines 1409-1410: "SetIdleHint() is called by the session object to update the idle state of the session whenever it changes" — all verbatim. man/logind.conf.xml lines 157-162 under IdleAction=: "Note that this requires that user sessions correctly report the idle status to the system. The system will execute the action after all sessions report that they are idle..." — verbatim. The inferential tail ("logind does not measure graphical idleness itself") is confirmed by src/login/logind-session.c at v261.2, session_get_idle_hint(): "Graphical sessions have an explicit idle hint" -> returns s->idle_hint as set by SetIdleHint; logind only measures idleness itself for TTY sessions via tty atime. Source is the upstream systemd repo at the stated tag (primary), claim is current for v261.2, and every quoted phrase matches.

Both halves verified against primary sources. (1) The cited X.org scrnsaverproto page is reachable (the URL 301-redirects www.x.org/releases/current -> www.x.org/archive/current -> xorg.freedesktop.org/archive/current; full 47,900-byte document retrieved). It is the X.org-published 'X11 Screen Saver Extension' spec (MIT X Consortium Proposed Standard, Jim Fulton & Keith Packard, X11R7.7, Version 1.0). Its ScreenSaverQueryInfo request description states verbatim: 'The idle field specifies the number of milliseconds since the last input was received from the user on any of the input devices.' The Xlib XScreenSaverQueryInfo section documents XScreenSaverInfo with 'unsigned long idle; /* milliseconds */' and cross-references that request for field meanings, so attributing the sentence to XScreenSaverQueryInfo is supported. Minor note, not a refutation: the spec prose says 'The name of this extension is "SCREEN-SAVER"', whereas the authoritative xorgproto header include/X11/extensions/saver.h line 31 defines ScreenSaverName "MIT-SCREEN-SAVER" -- the claim's label matches the real registered name. (2) xprintidle tag 0.3.0 exists (github.com/g0hl1n/xprintidle): meson.build declares version '0.3.0' and license 'GPL-2.0'; xprintidle.c carries 'SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-only' and 'under the terms of version 2 of the GNU General Public License' with no or-later clause; COPYING is the GPLv2 text -- so GPL-2.0-only is accurate. README.md at 0.3.0 (and the man page) say verbatim 'xprintidle is a utility that queries the X server for the user's idle time and prints it to stdout (in milliseconds).' It uses Xss: README lists 'X11, Xext and Xss libraries' as dependencies, meson.build has dependency('xscrnsaver'), and the source includes <X11/extensions/scrnsaver.h> and calls XScreenSaverQueryExtension/XScreenSaverAllocInfo/XScreenSaverQueryInfo. Caveat for the dossier (does not contradict the claim as stated): xprintidle.c contains a workaround noting that when DPMS is active the X server's XScreenSaverInfo->idle is not actually the time since last input, so the spec wording and real-world server behaviour can diverge.
