Fetched https://caddyserver.com/docs/caddyfile/directives/reverse_proxy (and its raw markdown at /docs/markdown/caddyfile/directives/reverse_proxy.md) on 2026-08-22; it is Caddy's official primary documentation. Verbatim matches: syntax `reverse_proxy [<matcher>] [<upstreams...>] {`; "By default, Caddy passes through incoming headers—including `Host`—to the backend without modifications, with three exceptions" (sets or augments X-Forwarded-For; sets X-Forwarded-Proto; sets X-Forwarded-Host); "For these `X-Forwarded-*` headers, by default, the proxy will ignore their values from incoming requests, to prevent spoofing."; recommendation to configure via the `servers > trusted_proxies` global option; `header_up   [+|-]<field> [<value|regexp> [<replacement>]]` and `header_down [+|-]<field> [<value|regexp> [<replacement>]]`; "To delete a request header, preventing it from reaching the backend: header_up -Some-Header"; upstream examples include `localhost:4000`, `http://localhost:4000`, `h2c://127.0.0.1`, `unix//var/php.sock`; `flush_interval` "adjusts how often Caddy should flush the response buffer to the client" under the streaming options. Only nuance: the docs say X-Forwarded-For is "set or augmented" while Proto/Host are "set" — the claim's "sets/augments" for all three is a harmless compression, not an error.

Fetched https://caddyserver.com/docs/caddyfile/directives/handle_path (primary, current Caddy v2 docs, 2026-08-22). The page says verbatim: "Works the same as the handle directive, but implicitly uses uri strip_prefix to strip the matched path prefix." It carries exactly the cited example (`handle_path /api/* { reverse_proxy localhost:9000 }` commented "Serve your API, stripping the /api prefix") and states `handle_path /prefix/*` is effectively `handle /prefix/*` + `uri strip_prefix /prefix`. Cross-checked against the primary handle page (https://caddyserver.com/docs/caddyfile/directives/handle): "handle_path does the same as handle, but it strips a prefix from the request before running its handlers" whereas plain handle preserves the full path — so the inference (handle_path when the status app is mounted at root; handle when the app knows its own /status prefix) follows from the source. ADR-0003 in the repo (docs/adr/0003-endpoints.md line 19) does route `/status` → `:8092`, so the application is accurate. One caveat worth carrying (not a refutation, as it concerns the matcher pattern rather than the directive choice): per https://caddyserver.com/docs/caddyfile/matchers, "/foo/* will not match /foo", so a `/status/*` matcher will not catch a bare `/status` request; use `/status*` or add a `redir /status /status/ 308` if bare `/status` must work.

Fetched https://caddyserver.com/docs/caddyfile/directives/forward_auth on 2026-08-22 (official Caddy v2 documentation, primary source, page footer © 2026). Every element of the claim is present verbatim or as a faithful paraphrase: the intro reads "An opinionated directive which proxies a clone of the request to an authentication gateway"; the behaviour list reads "If the upstream responds with a 2xx status code, then access is granted and the header fields in copy_headers are copied to the original request" and "Otherwise, if the upstream responds with any other status code, then the upstream's response is copied back to the client"; copy_headers is described as "a list of HTTP header fields to copy from the response to the original request, when the request has a success status code" with renaming "by using > followed by the new name, for example Before>After"; the page states the directive "is actually just a convenient way to use a longer, more common configuration" and "an opinionated wrapper over a reverse proxy" (i.e. sugar over reverse_proxy, with the expanded reverse_proxy form shown). The Tailscale example block matches the claim exactly: forward_auth unix//run/tailscale.nginx-auth.sock { uri /auth; header_up Remote-Addr {remote_host}; header_up Remote-Port {remote_port}; header_up Original-URI {uri}; copy_headers { Tailscale-User>X-Webauth-User, Tailscale-Name>X-Webauth-Name, Tailscale-Login>X-Webauth-Login, Tailscale-Tailnet>X-Webauth-Tailnet, Tailscale-Profile-Picture>X-Webauth-Profile-Picture } }. No discrepancy found; claim stands for the stated version.

Fetched https://caddyserver.com/docs/caddyfile/directives/bind (HTTP 200) and cross-checked against the docs' GitHub source (caddyserver/website, src/docs/markdown/caddyfile/directives/bind.md). Every quoted element matches verbatim: page opens "Overrides the interface to which the server's socket should bind."; syntax is `bind <hosts...>`; "Normally, the listener binds to the empty (wildcard) interface"; "bind accepts network addresses, but may not include a port" / "This directive accepts only a host, not a port. The port is determined by the site address (defaulting to 443)"; examples include `bind 127.0.0.1`, `bind 127.0.0.1 [::1]`, and `example.com:8080 { bind 10.0.0.1 }`; and the parenthetical "(Virtual hosts are not shared across different listeners.)" is present. The tail of the claim (which IP to bind in kernel vs userspace Tailscale mode) is an internal design inference cross-referenced to R07-F26, not a factual assertion about this source, so it is out of scope here; the doc does confirm that binding a specific IP such as the tailnet address or 127.0.0.1 is exactly what the directive does.

Fetched https://caddyserver.com/docs/caddyfile/directives/log (HTTP 200, 2026-08-22; official Caddy v2 docs = primary) and cross-checked the page's markdown source at raw.githubusercontent.com/caddyserver/website/master/src/docs/markdown/caddyfile/directives/log.md. Not refuted. Both cited sources are primary (Tailscale's own KB; Caddy's own docs) and were fetched directly on 2026-08-22. Caddy docs (https://caddyserver.com/docs/automatic-https, "Special cases") read verbatim: "Domains ending in .ts.net will not be managed by Caddy. Instead, Caddy will automatically attempt to get these certificates at handshake-time from the locally-running Tailscale instance. This requires that HTTPS is enabled in your Tailscale account and the Caddy process must either be running as root, or you must configure tailscaled to give your Caddy user permission to fetch certificates." Tailscale KB 1190 shows "Last validated: Jan 5, 2026" and reads verbatim: "Starting with the beta release of Caddy 2.5, Caddy supports Tailscale. When Caddy gets an HTTPS request for a *.ts.net site, it gets the HTTPS certificate from the machine's local Tailscale daemon... you can use a Caddyfile for a static file server, and it automatically enables HTTPS: machine-name.domain-alias.ts.net root * /var/www file_server" and "In /etc/default/tailscaled, set the TS_PERMIT_CERT_UID environment variable to the name or ID of the non-root user: TS_PERMIT_CERT_UID=caddy". Every element of the claim (quotes, version attribution, validation date, env var, file path, site-block name) matches the sources as stated; nothing is outdated for the stated versions. Minor note only: the "HTTPS is enabled in your Tailscale account" and root/tailscaled requirement appear in the Caddy docs, not the Tailscale KB (the KB only covers the non-root TS_PERMIT_CERT_UID step) — the claim attributes them correctly.

Fetched https://tailscale.com/kb/1153/enabling-https (raw HTML via curl plus WebFetch); page header reads "Last validated: Dec 10, 2025", matching the stated version. Every element of the claim is supported verbatim by this primary (Tailscale-authored) source: (1) Configure HTTPS step 2: "Enable MagicDNS if not already enabled for your tailnet"; (2) "Using tailscale cert (with sudo as needed), Tailscale will automatically request a certificate for this machine on this domain, using Let's Encrypt"; (3) "The certificates provided by Let's Encrypt have a 90 day expiry and require periodic renewal ... for any certificates that you create using tailscale cert, you are responsible for renewing the certificate. If a certificate is handled without the user initiating any file-based certificate installation, such as when using the Caddy integration of Tailscale, then the certificate will automatically be renewed without the user doing anything"; (4) "All TLS certificates on the web are recorded in the Certificate Transparency (CT) append-only public ledger ... Do not enable the HTTPS feature if any of your machine names contain sensitive information" (exact sentence present); (5) names are machine-name.tailNNNN.ts.net / e.g. monitoring.yak-bebop.ts.net; (6) "It is possible to frequently request a new certificate and exceed Let's Encrypt's rate limits. As a result, you may find yourself waiting 34 hours until you can try again." Minor nuance only: the source gives Caddy as one example ("such as") of non-file-based handling that auto-renews, not the sole exception, but the claim's "unless Caddy integrates" is a fair paraphrase and not contradicted.

Core facts check out, but the claim as stated is not fully supported by the cited page and overstates two points. (1) https://caddyserver.com/docs/running (fetched 2026-08-22) says: edit `sudo nano /etc/caddy/Caddyfile`; "The Caddy process will run as the caddy user"; "If using a config file, you can gracefully reload Caddy after making any changes: sudo systemctl reload caddy". It contains NO mention of the admin API or localhost:2019. That mechanism comes from other pages: /docs/command-line#caddy-reload ("Because this command uses the API, the admin endpoint must not be disabled"; "--address needs to be used if the admin endpoint is not listening on the default address and if it is different from the address in the provided config file") and /docs/api ("Default address: localhost:2019", changeable via CADDY_ADMIN or the config's admin block). The official unit (caddyserver/dist init/caddy.service) has User=caddy, Group=caddy, ExecStart=/usr/bin/caddy run --environ --config /etc/caddy/Caddyfile, ExecReload=/usr/bin/caddy reload --config /etc/caddy/Caddyfile --force — so reload reads the admin address from the Caddyfile; localhost:2019 is the default, not an invariant. Group=caddy is in the unit file, not stated on the cited page. (2) The import page (/docs/caddyfile/directives/import) does say verbatim "Includes a snippet or file, replacing this directive with the contents of the snippet or file", "it can appear anywhere in the Caddyfile", and shows `import sites-enabled/*`. But "CORVID can own a drop-in route file instead of editing the hub's existing Caddyfile" overstates: the stock dist Caddyfile (caddyserver/dist config/Caddyfile) has no import line, so the hub Caddyfile must be edited once to add e.g. `import corvid.d/*`; the page also notes globs are "always relative to the file the import appears in", hidden files are ignored, and "an empty glob pattern is not an error" but a missing specific file is.
verdicts.corrected_statement: Caddy Linux service: the official systemd unit (caddyserver/dist init/caddy.service) runs as User=caddy/Group=caddy with ExecStart=`caddy run --environ --config /etc/caddy/Caddyfile` and ExecReload=`caddy reload --config /etc/caddy/Caddyfile --force`; docs/running says to edit /etc/caddy/Caddyfile and apply with `sudo systemctl reload caddy` (never stop/start). `caddy reload` pushes the config through the admin API (which must not be disabled), reading the admin address from the config — default localhost:2019 (docs/api; overridable via CADDY_ADMIN or the admin global option). The `import` directive "includes a snippet or file, replacing this directive with the contents", is evaluated before parsing and "can appear anywhere in the Caddyfile" (including inside site blocks), and accepts globs, e.g. `import sites-enabled/*` (paths relative to the importing file; dot-files ignored; empty glob is not an error). The stock /etc/caddy/Caddyfile ships with no import line, so CORVID needs a one-time edit adding e.g. `import corvid.d/*` to the hub Caddyfile; thereafter CORVID owns its drop-in file(s) under /etc/caddy/corvid.d/ and never touches the hub's other config.

missing: Caddy site address vs bind (blocks Task 6 of the Phase 2 plan and Phase 1 Task 6): R07-F16 says the listener is wildcard by default but never states that the host part of a Caddyfile site address is only a Host-header matcher. Both plans write `http://<hub-tailnet-ipv4>:80 { … }` with no `bind` — that listens on 0.0.0.0:80 (violates CLAUDE.md §5.6 / ADR-0003 amendment) and only matches requests whose Host is the raw IP, so `http://solarplexus.<tailnet>.ts.net/` would get Caddy's empty no-match response. Needed: the exact pattern (`http://solarplexus.<tailnet>.ts.net, http://<ip> { bind <tailnet-ipv4> … }` or `:80 { bind … }`), whether a `.ts.net` site name with explicit `http://` still avoids Caddy's Tailscale cert attempt + HTTP→HTTPS redirect (automatic-HTTPS page: `http://` prefix disables it), and whether the hub's existing Caddyfile has `default_bind`/`auto_https`/`order` globals that interact.

Anti-spoofing of X-Corvid-User/X-Corvid-Name through Caddy forward_auth: R07-F15 does not say whether `copy_headers` replaces an existing request header of the same name (expanded form is `request_header X {rp.header.X}` inside `handle_response @good`) or what happens when the auth response omits it; and Caddy's default directive order puts `request_header` AFTER `forward_auth`, so a top-level `request_header -X-Corvid-User` would delete the legitimate value. Plan needs: the replace semantics, and that stripping client-sent X-Corvid-*/Tailscale-User-* must be done inside a `route {}` block (order preserved) ahead of forward_auth — spec §7 test 9 and plan Task 10 ('header spoofing impossible') depend on this.

Caddy access log vs identity (spec §7 test 9: 'X-Corvid-User never appears in the access log'): R07-F17 only covers Cookie/Authorization redaction. Missing: what the default JSON access log entry contains (request.headers — original request or post-request_header-modified? client_ip/remote_ip of the member, uri incl. query, user_id), that Tailscale-User-* headers injected by Serve WOULD be in it, and the `log { format filter { request>headers>X-Corvid-User delete … } }` / `log_skip` mechanism to keep identity values out.

How the whoami endpoint reaches tailscaled from inside the compose `api` container: the plan runs `tailscale whois --json` from a `python:3.12-slim` image with no tailscale CLI and no socket mount. R07-F25 gives the LocalAPI facts but not the container recipe: bind-mount `/var/run/tailscale/tailscaled.sock` (0666, read-only LocalAPI ok for any uid), call `GET /localapi/v0/whois?addr=` over the unix socket with `Host: local-tailscaled.sock` (httpx uds transport) or apt-install the CLI in the image; expected status codes (403 'whois access denied', 404 'no match for IP:port'); and whether LocalAPI whois at hub tailscale 1.98.4 behaves like 1.102.3.

Tagged hubs vs agent identity (contradiction the dossier does not resolve): ADR-0002 decision 3 tags solarplexus/optiplex/ahnoway `tag:hub`, R07 rec 4 says 'tag hubs only', but whois on a tagged node returns Tags and no UserProfile (R07-F24) → the agents on all three build nodes would get 401 and the Phase 2 exit ('three nodes live, greet the member by name') fails. Missing: what WhoIsResponse holds for a tagged node (UserProfile nil? Node.User = creator?), and the chosen rule — leave the three build nodes untagged in Phase 2, or let whoami map `tag:hub` + Node.StableID to an owner for heartbeat routes only.

Does whois resolve the hub's own traffic: the solarplexus agent heartbeats to the hub's own tailnet IP (Caddy bound there); in kernel mode the source is the hub's own 100.x via lo. Not stated whether `tailscale whois <own-ip>` / LocalAPI returns the self node + user (and what it returns if the hub is tagged). One of the three map nodes depends on it.

Stable member key: tailcfg.UserProfile comments mark LoginName as 'for display purposes only' while UserProfile.ID (UserID) is the stable identifier; R07-F24 lists only {Node, UserProfile, CapMap} without field names. The schema keys `owner_login text` and ADR-0001 hard-partitions data per member — the dossier should name the JSON fields (UserProfile.ID, LoginName, DisplayName, ProfilePicURL; Node.ID, StableID, Name, Tags) and say which is the partition key.

Source of 'inference utilisation' for the pool panel (spec D11 'inference slots busy'): R07 rec 2 says 'utilisation = currently assigned/used by CORVID work' without a data source. llama-server offers GET /slots (`--slots` default on; README now says prompt text is not included; `?fail_on_no_slot=1`) or `--metrics` Prometheus gauges (`llamacpp:requests_processing`, `llamacpp:requests_deferred`), while R06 rec 14 says run with `--no-slots`. Plan needs which endpoint/flag at b10581, polled by whom, and confirmation it carries no prompt text.

IPv6 on the tailnet: Tailscale nodes also have fd7a:… addresses and MagicDNS may answer AAAA; Caddy `bind <tailnet-ipv4>` only → clients trying v6 first get connection-refused (Happy-Eyeballs fallback) and X-Forwarded-For could be a v6 address if v6 is bound. Missing: does MagicDNS return AAAA for the hub, should Caddy bind both tailnet addresses, and does whois accept the v6 form (F24 says v4 or v6) — plus what the bind lint expects.

Plain-HTTP front door viability: the dossier weighs CT-log exposure but never asks whether browsers will force HTTPS for *.ts.net (HSTS preload). Checked 2026-08-22: hstspreload.org reports ts.net status 'unknown' (not preloaded), so http://solarplexus.<tailnet>.ts.net/ works in browsers — add as a fact so the plan can rely on it.

Hub Caddy deployment facts (already an open question, but both Phase 1 and Phase 2 plans assumed answers): R00's raw inspection log contains no Caddy evidence at all — only port 2019 — so package-vs-container, Caddy version (forward_auth ≥ 2.5.1, copy_headers `>` rename ≥ 2.6.x, .ts.net certs ≥ 2.5), Caddyfile path, existing site address/custom port and global options, whether the caddy service can bind :80 (CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE in the deb unit) and write /var/log/caddy, and — if it is a container — its network mode (127.0.0.1:809x upstreams and `bind <tailnet-ip>` only work with host networking) are all unverified; one founder command (`systemctl status caddy; caddy version; docker ps | grep -i caddy`) resolves it.

S-05 remains pending (listed in the dossier): headers on `serve --http`, Serve in userspace mode, `whois 127.0.0.1:<port>` on the forwarded connection, and the LoginName format (email vs `user@github`) — the plan's Task 6 keeps a conditional branch until it runs; note the S-05 card file `spikes/S-05-serve-identity-headers.md` referenced by the dossier does not exist in docs/research/spikes/.

research.dossier:
R08 — Chat front-end for Phase 1 (verified 2026-08-22, primary sources only)

SUMMARY VERDICT
- Phase 1 demo ("a friend gets a completion from a model spread across two houses"): llama-server's built-in Web UI is sufficient and costs zero extra services. It is MIT, ships inside the llama-server binary, stores each person's conversations in their own browser (IndexedDB), and has no login at all. It is single-user-by-design: no server-side per-user history, no identity. Bind llama-server to the tailnet interface (its default is 127.0.0.1:8080) and friends open http://solarplexus:8080.
- First member-facing chat (Phase 2 "bookmark the site"): Open WebUI v0.11.0 is the only candidate that satisfies all four asks at once — (a) zero-login via trusted headers (WEBUI_AUTH_TRUSTED_EMAIL_HEADER / _NAME_HEADER), with an official Tailscale Serve tutorial (Serve injects Tailscale-User-Login / Tailscale-User-Name); (b) per-user chat history (SQLite, one container, default DATABASE_URL=sqlite:///{DATA_DIR}/webui.db); (c) telemetry already off in the official image (SCARF_NO_ANALYTICS=true, DO_NOT_TRACK=true, ANONYMIZED_TELEMETRY=false; ENABLE_OTEL default False) with ENABLE_VERSION_UPDATE_CHECK / ENABLE_COMMUNITY_SHARING / OFFLINE_MODE knobs; (d) single compose service. Licence caveat: since ~v0.6 it is NOT MIT — it is the "Open WebUI License", BSD-3-Clause plus a clause-4 branding restriction that is waived for deployments with ≤50 end users in any rolling 30-day period (CORVID qualifies; we would not rebrand anyway). Privacy caveat: ENABLE_ADMIN_CHAT_ACCESS defaults True (admins can read every user's chats) — set False or disclose per §5.7.
- LibreChat v0.8.7 (MIT): no trusted-header auth exists in a release — the feature is an open, unmerged PR (#8562, opened 2025-07-20; issue #1856 still open). Its compose needs MongoDB (+ rag_api by depends_on) — not a single service. OIDC is supported, so a future zero-login path is Tailscale's tsidp (experimental). Defer.
- Lobe Chat (repo now lobehub/lobehub, v2.2.14): "LobeHub Community License" (Apache 2.0 + extra conditions: derivative works need a commercial licence; producer may tighten terms). Auth is Better Auth (email/password, OAuth/OIDC providers), sessions in the DB; no trusted-header mode documented; minimum three services (app + PostgreSQL/pgvector + S3/RustFS). Not a fit.
- Hollama 0.35.4 (MIT): runs entirely in the browser, no accounts, history per browser, one container (ghcr.io/fmaclen/hollama, port 4173), supports OpenAI-compatible servers, no analytics packages declared. A fine zero-backend alternative to the llama.cpp UI, but "per-user history" is just "per-browser".
- Also checked: AnythingLLM (MIT; multi-user Docker-only; telemetry ON by default, DISABLE_TELEMETRY=true to stop), Hugging Face chat-ui (Apache-2.0; MongoDB-backed, OPENAI_BASE_URL only). Neither documents header auth; neither beats Open WebUI for this use.

ZERO-LOGIN MECHANISM (verified): Tailscale Serve proxies to a local port and adds Tailscale-User-Login, Tailscale-User-Name, Tailscale-User-Profile-Pic; it strips those headers from incoming requests (anti-spoofing); headers are absent for Funnel traffic and for tagged devices; the backend must be reachable only via Serve (listen on localhost / publish the container port on 127.0.0.1). Tailscale Serve requires HTTPS certificates enabled on the tailnet. Alternative identity sources: `tailscale whois --json <ip>` (CLI) and tsidp (experimental OIDC IdP, BSD-3, ghcr.io/tailscale/tsidp).

RISK FLAGGED FOR THE HUB: solarplexus runs tailscaled with --tun=userspace-networking. Tailscale's userspace-networking and Serve docs do not state whether Serve works in that mode (neither yes nor no). This must be spiked before the Open WebUI + Serve design is committed; the Open WebUI tutorial's tailscale-sidecar compose pattern is the documented fallback.

facts.statement: Open WebUI's latest GitHub release is v0.11.0, published 2026-07-27T09:30:15Z.

The LICENSE file at tag v0.11.0 is titled "Open WebUI License", "Copyright (c) 2023- Open WebUI Inc. [Created by Timothy Jaeryang Baek]"; it follows BSD-3-Clause structure plus clause 4: licensees are "strictly prohibited from altering, removing, obscuring, or replacing any 'Open WebUI' branding" except (i) deployments where total end users do not exceed fifty (50) within any rolling thirty (30) day period, (ii) prior written permission, or (iii) an enterprise license; clause 5: prior materials keep their terms per LICENSE_HISTORY; contributors agree to a CLA. It is not MIT.

LICENSE_HISTORY at v0.11.0 states earlier code was MIT (materials created before commit a76068d69cd59568b920dfab85dc573dbbb8f131) and BSD-3-Clause (materials created before commit 60d84a3aae9802339705826e9095e272e3c83623); boundaries are given as commits, not version numbers.

Open WebUI supports trusted-header (reverse-proxy) authentication: WEBUI_AUTH_TRUSTED_EMAIL_HEADER names the header whose value is used as the user's email, "handling automatic registration and login"; WEBUI_AUTH_TRUSTED_NAME_HEADER sets the display name (email used if unset); WEBUI_AUTH_TRUSTED_GROUPS_HEADER syncs comma-separated groups; WEBUI_AUTH_TRUSTED_ROLE_HEADER sets role. Warning: "Incorrect configuration can allow users to authenticate as any user... Make sure to allow only the authenticating proxy access to Open WebUI, such as by not opening any ports directly to the container, or by setting HOST=127.0.0.1". Docs list Tailscale Serve, Cloudflare Access, oauth2-proxy, Authentik, Authelia as supported proxies.
facts.version: docs main as of 2026-08-22; env vars defined (default None) in backend/open_webui/env.py at v0.11.0

facts.statement: Open WebUI's official Tailscale tutorial: "When a request passes through `tailscale serve`, Tailscale automatically sets the `Tailscale-User-Login` header with the email address of the authenticated user"; set WEBUI_AUTH_TRUSTED_EMAIL_HEADER=Tailscale-User-Login and WEBUI_AUTH_TRUSTED_NAME_HEADER=Tailscale-User-Name; example `sudo tailscale serve https / http://localhost:8080`; it also shows a compose with a tailscale/tailscale sidecar + serve.json proxying to http://open-webui:8080. Caveat quoted: "If you run Tailscale in the same network context as Open WebUI, users could bypass the Serve proxy and reach Open WebUI directly, skipping the trusted header authentication."

Open WebUI hardening guide: "When using trusted headers, your proxy must strip these headers from incoming client requests before injecting its own values. If the proxy does not strip them, any client can send a forged header and authenticate as any user." Also: "Signup is open only until the first user registers, who becomes the administrator. After that, signup is automatically disabled." OFFLINE_MODE "disables HuggingFace Hub downloads, version update checks, and other outbound calls".

Per-user history isolation in Open WebUI is qualified by admin access: ENABLE_ADMIN_CHAT_ACCESS (default True) "Controls whether the admin-panel other-users-chats access surface is available" (admins can view all user chats) and ENABLE_ADMIN_EXPORT (default True) controls admin export of data/chats/database. DEFAULT_USER_ROLE defaults to `pending` (new users need admin approval); ENABLE_SIGNUP defaults True.
facts.version: docs main as of 2026-08-22; DEFAULT_USER_ROLE/ENABLE_SIGNUP defaults confirmed in backend/open_webui/config.py at v0.11.0

facts.statement: The official Open WebUI Dockerfile at v0.11.0 sets `SCARF_NO_ANALYTICS=true DO_NOT_TRACK=true ANONYMIZED_TELEMETRY=false` and `EXPOSE 8080`; .env.example at v0.11.0 sets the same three values.

Open WebUI backend defaults at v0.11.0 (env.py/config.py): WEBUI_AUTH=True; DATABASE_URL = f'sqlite:///{DATA_DIR}/webui.db'; DATA_DIR = BACKEND_DIR/'data'; OFFLINE_MODE=false; ENABLE_VERSION_UPDATE_CHECK=true; ENABLE_OTEL=False; ENABLE_COMMUNITY_SHARING=True; ENABLE_OPENAI_API=True; ENABLE_OLLAMA_API=True; OPENAI_API_BASE_URL='' (empty entries resolve to https://api.openai.com/v1; multiple URLs via OPENAI_API_BASE_URLS separated by ';').

Open WebUI deploys as one container: docs state "Out of the box, Open WebUI runs as a single container with: An embedded SQLite database stored on a local volume" (PostgreSQL/Redis only needed for multiple instances/workers); quick start command is `docker run -d -p 3000:8080 -v open-webui:/app/backend/data --name open-webui ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui:main`; "The first account created gets Administrator privileges". The repo docker-compose.yaml defines two services (ollama + open-webui) but the ollama service is only a model runtime and is not required.
facts.version: docs main as of 2026-08-22; compose at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/open-webui/open-webui/main/docker-compose.yaml

facts.statement: Open WebUI docs recommend pinning release tags (`ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui:vX.Y.Z`) instead of `:main`, which "always points to the latest build... can include breaking changes without warning"; data lives in the `open-webui` volume (/app/backend/data).

A container image tag exactly `ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui:v0.11.0` exists — NOT confirmed: the GHCR package pages fetched showed only git-<sha>/dev tags in the visible slice (37,912 tagged versions total). Verify at build time with `docker manifest inspect`.
LibreChat's newest non-prerelease GitHub release is v0.8.7 (published 2026-06-24T19:41:03Z); v0.8.8-rc1 (2026-08-14) is marked prerelease.
LibreChat LICENSE at tag v0.8.7 is the MIT License, "Copyright (c) 2026 LibreChat".

LibreChat has no trusted-header / reverse-proxy identity auth: the docs' Authentication page lists email/local, social, OAuth2/OIDC, LDAP/AD, SAML only; PR #8562 "feat: add support for reverse proxy auth headers" (closes #1856) is state=open, merged=false, created 2025-07-20; the dotenv reference's only proxy-related var is TRUST_PROXY (default 1, Express hop count).

LibreChat's docker-compose.yml at v0.8.7 defines six services — api (registry.librechat.ai/danny-avila/librechat-dev:latest), admin-panel, mongodb (mongo:8.0.20), meilisearch (getmeili/meilisearch:v1.35.1), vectordb (pgvector/pgvector:0.8.0-pg15-trixie), rag_api — and `api` has `depends_on: - mongodb - rag_api`; MONGO_URI is required (docs give no optional designation) while Meilisearch search is "disabled by default"; PORT default 3080. Not deployable as a single compose service.

LibreChat points at any OpenAI-compatible server through librechat.yaml custom endpoints (fields name, apiKey, baseURL, models.default/fetch, titleConvo); it "appends '/chat/completions'... to the baseURL by default".

LibreChat's documented observability is opt-in: Langfuse (needs keys), OTEL_TRACING_ENABLED, RUM_ENABLED (default false; RUM console capture "May collect sensitive prompts, responses, or payloads"), and MEILI_NO_ANALYTICS=true for Meilisearch. No first-party phone-home telemetry is documented; the absence of undocumented telemetry was not independently verified.

LibreChat supports generic OpenID Connect via OPENID_CLIENT_ID, OPENID_CLIENT_SECRET, OPENID_ISSUER, OPENID_SESSION_SECRET, OPENID_SCOPE, OPENID_CALLBACK_URL (default /oauth/openid/callback), OPENID_AUTO_REDIRECT, OPENID_REQUIRED_ROLE, OPENID_USERNAME_CLAIM, OPENID_NAME_CLAIM — a possible future zero-login path via Tailscale tsidp (see R08-F31).

The lobehub/lobe-chat repository now resolves to full_name lobehub/lobehub (default branch canary); GitHub reports license spdx_id NOASSERTION / "Other"; latest release v2.2.14 published 2026-08-16T07:02:43Z.

Lobe Chat/LobeHub LICENSE at v2.2.14 is the "LobeHub Community License" ("Copyright (c) 2024/06/17 - current LobeHub LLC"): based on Apache 2.0 with additional conditions — commercial use as a frontend/backend service without modifying source is allowed, but "a commercial license must be obtained from the producer if you want to develop and distribute a derivative work"; contributors accept that "The producer can adjust the open-source agreement to be more strict or relaxed".

LobeHub v2.2.14 self-hosted auth uses Better Auth: email/password, magic links, Google/GitHub/Microsoft/Apple/AWS Cognito, and OIDC providers (Auth0, Authelia, Authentik, Casdoor, Cloudflare Zero Trust, Keycloak, Logto, Okta, ZITADEL, Generic OIDC, Feishu, WeChat); required AUTH_SECRET and APP_URL; AUTH_SSO_PROVIDERS, AUTH_DISABLE_EMAIL_PASSWORD, AUTH_ALLOWED_EMAILS; "Better Auth uses the database to store session data". No trusted-header / reverse-proxy identity mode is documented.

LobeHub v2.2.14 Docker Compose deployment requires "at least the following three services": LobeHub app (port 3210), PostgreSQL with PGVector plugin, and an S3-compatible object store (RustFS, ports 9000/9001), plus optional Casdoor/Logto for SSO; start.mdx says "PostgreSQL 14+ is required". No single-container mode is documented.

LobeHub v2.2.14 analytics are env-gated: ENABLE_VERCEL_ANALYTICS, GOOGLE_ANALYTICS_MEASUREMENT_ID, POSTHOG_KEY (POSTHOG_HOST defaults to https://app.posthog.com), UMAMI_WEBSITE_ID — off unless set; ENABLE_LANGFUSE is documented as default 1 but requires LANGFUSE_* keys (LANGFUSE_HOST default https://cloud.langfuse.com).
Hollama's latest release is 0.35.4 (2025-10-12); LICENSE at that tag is MIT, "Copyright (c) 2023 Fernando Maclen".

Hollama is "A minimal LLM chat app that runs entirely in your browser" with "Support for Ollama & OpenAI servers", "Multi-server support", "Stores data locally on your browser", "Import & export stored data", "No sign-up required"; self-host with `docker run --rm -d -p 4173:4173 --name hollama ghcr.io/fmaclen/hollama:latest` (env OLLAMA_ORIGINS, VITE_ALLOWED_HOSTS). There are no user accounts: history is per-browser, not per-user on the server.

Hollama's package.json at 0.35.4 declares no analytics/telemetry packages (dependencies: esbuild, wrangler; devDependencies are build/UI tooling incl. ollama, openai, svelte) — no @vercel/analytics, posthog, plausible, sentry, umami.

llama.cpp's latest release is v0.2.0 (published 2026-08-21T18:32:48Z), which "marks the beginning of consistent semantic versioning": tag vX.Y.Z = stable, recommended for downstream distribution; tag b[NUM] = bleeding edge. LICENSE at v0.2.0 is MIT, "Copyright (c) 2023-2026 The ggml authors".

llama-server (v0.2.0) ships a built-in Web UI: `--ui, --webui, --no-ui, --no-webui` "whether to enable the Web UI (default: enabled)"; "You can visit the web front end at the same url"; `--path PATH` serves custom static files; defaults --host 127.0.0.1, --port 8080; `--api-key KEY` (comma-separated list) / `--api-key-file`; `--rpc SERVERS` comma-separated RPC servers; OpenAI-compatible endpoints include GET /v1/models, POST /v1/chat/completions, /v1/completions, /v1/embeddings, /v1/responses; --metrics default disabled; --slots default enabled.

The llama-server Web UI (source in tools/ui/ at v0.2.0; SvelteKit) is compiled into the llama-server binary and served at the root path; it stores "IndexedDB: Conversations and messages" (via Dexie) and "LocalStorage: Settings, user parameter overrides, theme" — all client-side; the README documents no authentication, accounts, or multi-user support.

Tailscale Serve adds identity headers to proxied requests: Tailscale-User-Login (e.g. alice@example.com), Tailscale-User-Name, Tailscale-User-Profile-Pic; "If Serve finds the following headers on an incoming request, it will remove them for security reasons, to avoid header spoofing"; "These identity headers are not populated for traffic originating from tagged devices"; Funnel traffic does not include identity headers; best practice: "only have the service listen on localhost"; "Tailscale Serve requires you to enable HTTPS certificates in your tailnet"; basic command `tailscale serve 3000` (HTTP variant: `tailscale serve --http=80 localhost:3000`).

tsidp is Tailscale's OIDC/OAuth identity provider for a tailnet: "tsidp is an experimental project. It is under active development and might experience breaking changes"; identity comes from LocalAPI whois; supports Dynamic Client Registration; runs as ghcr.io/tailscale/tsidp:latest with persistent TS_STATE_DIR; LICENSE is BSD 3-Clause, "Copyright (c) 2025 Tailscale Inc & AUTHORS".

`tailscale whois <ip>` returns "the machine and user associated with a Tailscale IP" and `--json` gives machine-readable output — usable by a CORVID-side proxy/agent to map a connecting tailnet IP to a member without any login.

recommendations: Phase 1 exit demo: use llama-server's built-in Web UI (MIT, inside the binary) — no extra service. Start llama-server with --host <solarplexus tailnet IP> (default is 127.0.0.1) and --rpc <workers>; friends open http://solarplexus:8080. Accept that history is per-browser and there is no identity; do not set --api-key for the demo (the UI is open to the tailnet, which is the security boundary per CLAUDE.md §3.2).

Member-facing chat (Phase 2 'bookmark the site'): adopt Open WebUI, pinned to a vX.Y.Z tag (v0.11.0 today; verify the GHCR tag exists — R08-F12), one container, SQLite on the open-webui volume, published on 127.0.0.1:8080 only, fronted by `tailscale serve` on solarplexus. Env: WEBUI_AUTH_TRUSTED_EMAIL_HEADER=Tailscale-User-Login, WEBUI_AUTH_TRUSTED_NAME_HEADER=Tailscale-User-Name, DEFAULT_USER_ROLE=user (else friends land 'pending'), OPENAI_API_BASE_URL=http://<llama-server>:8080/v1 with a dummy OPENAI_API_KEY, ENABLE_OLLAMA_API=false, ENABLE_COMMUNITY_SHARING=false, ENABLE_VERSION_UPDATE_CHECK=false (or OFFLINE_MODE=true if RAG downloads are not wanted), ENABLE_ADMIN_CHAT_ACCESS=false and ENABLE_ADMIN_EXPORT=false (or disclose per §5.7 that the admin can read chats).

Record Open WebUI in CLAUDE.md §4 as 'Open WebUI License (BSD-3-Clause + branding clause)', not MIT; note CORVID's ≤50-end-users exemption (clause 4(i)) and the house rule: never rebrand it. Write ADR 'chat front-end' capturing this choice and the rejected options (LibreChat: no header auth in any release, MongoDB+rag_api; Lobe: custom licence + 3-service minimum + no header auth).

Before committing to the Serve design, run a spike on solarplexus: does `tailscale serve` work under --tun=userspace-networking and do the Tailscale-User-* headers arrive at a local listener (curl a tiny echo server)? If not, use the Open WebUI tutorial's tailscale-sidecar compose pattern (tailscale/tailscale container + serve.json -> http://open-webui:8080) or a tiny Python proxy that calls `tailscale whois --json` and injects the header itself.

Header-spoofing guard as a CI/ops check (ties to §5.6): the Open WebUI container must never be published on 0.0.0.0; only the Serve path may reach it. Tailscale Serve strips incoming Tailscale-User-* headers, but only if every request really goes through Serve.

Shared/tagged-device caveat: identity headers are not populated for tagged devices; design member nodes as user-owned (untagged) devices, and test what header value a member who logged into Tailscale with GitHub (non-email login) produces before relying on it as an 'email'.

Keep Hollama (MIT, one container, browser-local data) as the documented zero-backend fallback if Open WebUI ever feels heavy; keep LibreChat on the watch list keyed to PR #8562 merging or tsidp leaving 'experimental' (OIDC path). Do not adopt Lobe Chat.

Telemetry statement for members: Open WebUI's official image already ships SCARF_NO_ANALYTICS=true, DO_NOT_TRACK=true, ANONYMIZED_TELEMETRY=false, ENABLE_OTEL off; what remains outbound is the version check (disable) and any HF model downloads for RAG/STT (document or set OFFLINE_MODE).

research.dossier:
R09 — SharedLLM & alternatives (verified 2026-08-22, primary sources only)

HEADLINE
None of the five candidates coordinates stock llama.cpp RPC workers across a Linux+macOS+Windows fleet today. The one that did (SharedLLM) has taken its source private and pivoted to a closed macOS desktop node that auto-joins a public global fleet; GPUStack dropped llama.cpp/llama-box and macOS/Windows workers in v2.0.0; exo 1.x is MLX-only (macOS GPU, Linux CPU, no Windows) and has gone quiet; prima.cpp is a research fork of llama.cpp with its own ring parallelism, no releases, no Windows; Ollama is single-host by design. CORVID's plan to keep a small Python+Postgres coordinator of its own around llama.cpp RPC stands — and CLAUDE.md §3.2's "Phase 5 mandate: evaluate adopting/contributing to SharedLLM" needs an ADR, because there is nothing public to adopt or contribute to.

SHAREDLLM (sharedllm.org; source repo MHASK/sharedllm — now private)
- What it was: v0.1.0 "public alpha" announced 2026-04-11 — Python coordinator + node daemon (sharedllm-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl) wrapping stock llama.cpp rpc-server/llama-server binaries (shipped for macOS arm64/Metal, Linux x86_64, Linux arm64, Windows x86_64), HMAC-SHA256 cluster secret, worker discovery, free-memory tracking, split planning, re-planning on node drop. Its own words: only the tiny stories260K model verified end-to-end; larger quants hit an upstream RPC assertion; "If you need a production-grade mesh today, SharedLLM is not that project."
- What it is now: github.com/MHASK/sharedllm returns 404 (web and API). The only public artifact is MHASK/sharedllm-releases, whose README says "Source code lives in the private MHASK/sharedllm repo. This repo holds binaries only." Releases v0.1.0 (2026-06-08), v0.2.0 and v0.2.1 (2026-06-10) are macOS Apple Silicon .dmg only; v0.2.0 notes: zero-config, "the app joins the sharedllm.org fleet on first launch", RAM/disk capped at 2 GB. sharedllm.org footer: "An open-source initiative from Naridon, Inc. ... License: AGPLv3 | Source Code on GitHub", "Currently in beta with live nodes." The AGPL-3.0-or-later claim cannot be verified against any LICENSE file at any tag. No PyPI package (pypi.org/pypi/sharedllm → 404).
- Verdict for CORVID: not adoptable, not contributable, and its current direction (closed node, public global fleet, auto-join) conflicts with §1/§5/§7 (friends-only, opt-in, zero public exposure). Keep it as *prior art for design ideas* (HMAC-authenticated RPC proxy, free-memory tracking, re-plan on drop) credited to its blog posts, and record the pivot in an ADR. (Aside: its April-2026 comparison table lists exo as GPL-3.0/tinygrad — stale; see exo.)

EXO (exo-explore/exo)
- Latest release v1.0.71, 2026-04-23; no newer release or prerelease. LICENSE at v1.0.71: Apache-2.0, "Copyright 2025 Exo Technologies Ltd". The repo was GPL-3.0 from 2024-07-16 through at least v0.0.15-alpha (2025-02-25); the licence changed during "prep repo for v1" (2025-12-17/18).
- Matrix at v1.0.71: MLX backend + MLX distributed; macOS uses the GPU (app requires macOS Tahoe 26.2+; RDMA over Thunderbolt 5); "Currently, exo runs on CPU on Linux. GPU support for Linux platforms is under development." No mention of Windows, CUDA, NVIDIA, AMD or llama.cpp anywhere in the README. Own sharding: auto-discovery, tensor parallelism (claimed 1.8x/3.2x on 2/4 devices), topology-aware auto parallel, MlxRing pipeline.
- Linux CUDA: tracking issue #913 open since 2025-12-18 (last update 2026-02-02). The pre-1.0 tinygrad engine that gave Linux/NVIDIA support was dropped in the v1 rewrite. Scottcjn/exo-cuda is an independent GPL-3.0 repo ("CUDA support via tinygrad", Linux only, CUDA 12.0+/driver 525+, v1.0.0 2026-01-02, 92 stars, still pushed 2026-08-20) descended from the GPL-era code — it is not a CUDA port of exo 1.x, and its licence differs from upstream's.
- Maturity: 46,960 stars; last commit 2026-06-22; issue #2258 "Is this repository even actively being watched and maintained…" (2026-08-03) open with 13 comments and no maintainer reply visible.
- Verdict: Mac-only experiment at best (Apple-Silicon friends), as CLAUDE.md already says; §3.2's sentence about the CUDA fork should be corrected (GPL-3.0, tinygrad, pre-1.0 lineage).

GPUSTACK (gpustack/gpustack)
- Latest v2.2.3, 2026-07-31 (2026 cadence: 2.1.0 Mar-07 … 2.2.0 Jun-18, 2.2.1, 2.2.2, 2.2.3). LICENSE at v2.2.3: Apache-2.0, "Copyright (c) 2024 The GPUStack authors". Very active (last commit 2026-08-21; ≥100 commits since 2026-05-01; 5,535 stars; 684 open issues).
- Matrix: README v2.2.3 — "Only Linux is supported for GPUStack worker nodes. If you use Windows, consider using WSL2 and avoid using Docker Desktop. macOS is not supported for GPUStack worker nodes." Docs 2.2 (=latest): Linux AMD64/ARM64 only; NVIDIA needs a driver supporting CUDA 12.8+ plus NVIDIA Container Toolkit (solarplexus at driver 535/CUDA 12.2 fails this); AMD ROCm 7.0+; plus Ascend/Hygon/MThreads/Iluvatar/MetaX/Cambricon/T-Head.
- llama.cpp: "llama-box is no longer supported as of v2.0.0. Use llama.cpp via the custom inference backend instead." and "Distributed inference across multiple workers is currently not supported with custom inference backends." Built-in backends are vLLM, SGLang, MindIE, VoxBox; cross-worker distribution is "(Experimental)" via Ray sidecar or vLLM multiprocessing, Linux-only nodes. So GPUStack neither coordinates llama.cpp RPC nor runs on our Mac/Windows members.
- Verdict: off the v1 candidate list; keep only as a pattern source (cluster UI, Prometheus/Grafana pairing).

PRIMA.CPP
- The seed URL github.com/Lizonghang/prima.cpp is dead (404; user Lizonghang also 404). The ICLR 2026 paper's arXiv v3 (2026-07-04) points to github.com/OpenCPIL/prima.cpp ("[Official] prima.cpp…"), an org repo created 2026-06-30 by "Initial import" — history reset; 8 commits all on 2026-06-30; 0 tags; 0 releases; 81 stars; one contributor (zonghang-li). MIT ("Copyright (c) 2023-2024 The ggml authors and 2024-2025 the prima.cpp authors."). Only version-like identifiers: Docker Hub lizonghango00o1/prima.cpp:1.0.0-cuda (2025-04-08), 1.0.1-cuda, 1.0.2-cuda (2025-06-26).
- Mechanism: "a distributed implementation of llama.cpp" (fork) with its own pipelined-ring parallelism over ZeroMQ and HiGHS-based workload planning; launched as `llama-cli … --world 4 --rank 0 --master <ip> --next <ip> --prefetch`. No mention of llama.cpp's RPC backend.
- Matrix: Linux, macOS (Metal), Android/HarmonyOS via Termux; CUDA-only GPUs; "Does it support Windows? Not yet—but it's on the roadmap."; Vulkan/AMD on roadmap. Peer-reviewed (ICLR 2026 poster) but a research prototype.
- Verdict: watch-list only; update the URL in CLAUDE.md.

OLLAMA
- Latest stable v0.32.15 (2026-08-19); v0.33.0-rc2 prerelease 2026-08-21; 12 stable releases between 2026-07-23 and 2026-08-19; 72 commits since 2026-08-01; 179,162 stars. LICENSE at v0.32.15: MIT, "Copyright (c) Ollama".
- Matrix at v0.32.15: macOS Sonoma 14+ ("Apple M series (CPU and GPU support) or x86 (CPU only)"); Windows; Linux amd64/arm64 (install.sh + systemd); Docker. NVIDIA: "compute capability 5.0+ and driver version 550 and newer"; "compute capability 5.0 through 6.2 require driver version 570 or newer" — the doc's own table puts GTX 970 at CC 5.2, RTX 2070 at 7.5, RTX 3050 at 8.6, so solarplexus (GTX 970, driver 535) is below Ollama's documented minimum. AMD ROCm v7 (Linux) / ROCm v7-HIP7 (Windows); Vulkan on Windows/Linux; Metal on Apple. Engines: llama.cpp (README "Supported backends") plus an MLX engine "enabled by default" on macOS arm64 (docs/development.md); CUDA builds cuda_v12/cuda_v13.
- Distribution: single host only — FAQ describes spreading a model across GPUs "in your system"; feature request #4643 "Llama.cpp now supports distributed inference across multiple machines." open since 2024-05-26 (67 reactions, 48 comments, last activity 2026-06-11).
- Verdict: remains the single-node UX bar; not a coordinator.

UPSTREAM NOTE THAT AFFECTS THE SPEC
llama.cpp renamed the RPC worker binary: commit c299a92c38 (2026-06-27, "binaries : Improve rpc-server and export-graph-ops names. (#25045)"); tools/rpc/README.md on master now documents `ggml-rpc-server` (builds with -DGGML_RPC=ON, `-p 50052`, `--device CUDA0`), `llama-server/llama-cli --rpc host:port,…`, splitting "in proportion to each device's available memory" with `--tensor-split` override, and "Never run the RPC server on an open network or in a sensitive environment!" Also: GitHub's "latest" llama.cpp release is now a semver tag v0.2.0 (2026-08-21) while b-builds (b10581, 2026-08-22) are marked prerelease — Phase 1 must pin one explicitly.

facts.statement: SharedLLM v0.1.0 'public alpha' was announced 2026-04-11 as 'a community-owned AI compute mesh built on llama.cpp RPC'; the release comprised a Python coordinator + node daemon (sharedllm-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl + sdist) and pre-built rpc-server/llama-server bundles for macOS Apple Silicon (Metal), Linux x86_64, Linux arm64 and Windows x86_64; coordinator/worker handshake uses an HMAC-SHA256 cluster secret.

SharedLLM's own description of its coordinator: it 'discovers workers, tracks each one's free memory, builds the split for you, re-plans when a machine drops, and wraps the raw RPC socket in an authenticated (HMAC-SHA256) proxy' around stock llama.cpp rpc-server and llama-server — i.e. it coordinates llama.cpp RPC workers rather than shipping its own sharding engine.

SharedLLM's own maturity statement at v0.1.0: 'Only the tiny stories260K test model is verified end-to-end cross-container; larger quantized models hit a known upstream llama.cpp RPC assertion on certain tensor shapes'; 'If you need a production-grade mesh today, SharedLLM is not that project.' Governance claimed: AGPL-3.0-or-later, DCO not CLA, non-profit.

The SharedLLM source repository linked from every sharedllm.org page, https://github.com/MHASK/sharedllm, returns HTTP 404 on github.com and via the GitHub REST API; a GitHub repository search for 'sharedllm' returns no public repository belonging to the project; pypi.org/pypi/sharedllm also returns 404.

MHASK/sharedllm-releases (created 2026-06-08, no LICENSE, 0 stars) states verbatim: 'Source code lives in the private MHASK/sharedllm repo. This repo holds binaries only.' Its releases are v0.1.0 (2026-06-08), v0.2.0 (2026-06-10) and v0.2.1 (2026-06-10), each shipping only SharedLLM-<ver>-aarch64.dmg / .app.tar.gz (macOS Apple Silicon) plus latest.json; v0.2.1 is the newest release.

SharedLLM v0.2.0 release notes (2026-06-10): 'Zero-config release. The app measures its own hardware and quietly sets aside a small slice — RAM-capped at 2 GB, disk-capped at 2 GB — to help the network' and 'Auto-join — the app joins the sharedllm.org fleet on first launch' — the project has pivoted to a closed desktop node that joins a public global fleet.

sharedllm.org states 'SharedLLM — An open-source initiative from Naridon, Inc. ... License: AGPLv3 | Source Code on GitHub © 2026 Naridon, Inc.' and 'Currently in beta with live nodes'; however no LICENSE file is publicly reachable at any tag (source repo is private), so the AGPL-3.0-or-later licence is a website claim only and cannot be verified at a pinned version.
GitHub user MHASK (public profile name 'Muhammed Ashique Kuthini', blog naridon.com) owns sharedllm-releases; none of the account's 22 public repositories contains SharedLLM source code.

exo's latest release is v1.0.71, published 2026-04-23 (not a prerelease); no newer release or prerelease exists as of 2026-08-22. Preceding releases: v1.0.70 (2026-04-17), v1.0.69 (2026-03-27), v1.0.68 (2026-02-25), v1.0.67 (2026-01-28).

Drop GPUStack from the inference-coordination candidate list for v1 and keep it on the watch list for UI/observability patterns only: workers are Linux-only (macOS/Windows dropped in v2.0.0), NVIDIA needs a CUDA 12.8+-capable driver (solarplexus at 535/CUDA 12.2 fails), llama-box was removed in v2.0.0 and a custom llama.cpp backend cannot span workers (R09-F19–F22).

verdicts.reason: Fetched the cited source directly (HTTP 200, sharedllm.org — the project's own site, so primary). Every element of the claim is supported verbatim: title "Announcing SharedLLM v0.1.0 — public alpha", datePublished 2026-04-11; the JSON-LD description reads "First public alpha of SharedLLM, a community-owned AI compute mesh built on llama.cpp RPC." (body prose: "a global, community-owned AI compute mesh"); "What's in the release" lists rpc-binaries-darwin-arm64.tar.gz (macOS Apple Silicon, Metal + RPC), rpc-binaries-linux-arm64.tar.gz, rpc-binaries-linux-x86_64.tar.gz, rpc-binaries-windows-x86_64.zip (mingw-w64 cross-compile), and "sharedllm-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl + sdist — the Python coordinator and node daemon"; "What actually works" lists "Coordinator + worker handshake with HMAC-SHA256 cluster secret." The project's own installer (https://sharedllm.org/install.sh, VERSION default v0.1.0) confirms the bundles contain "llama.cpp rpc-server + llama-server binaries (extracted from release tarball)" (binary names rpc-server and llama-server-rpc). Two caveats, neither refuting the claim as stated: (1) the GitHub repo/release page the post links to (github.com/MHASK/sharedllm, releases/tag/v0.1.0) returns 404 as of 2026-08-22 and the package is not on PyPI, so the artifacts themselves cannot currently be independently downloaded/verified — only the announcement text; (2) the exact quoted tagline comes from the page's meta description, not the body prose. Licence stated as AGPL-3.0-or-later.

Fetched https://sharedllm.org/blog/llama-cpp-rpc-distributed-inference.html (primary: SharedLLM's own site; JSON-LD datePublished/dateModified 2026-07-18, author "SharedLLM contributors"; page dateline "2026-07-18 · Tutorial"). The post contains the quoted sentence verbatim: "a coordinator that discovers workers, tracks each one's free memory, builds the split for you, re-plans when a machine drops, and wraps the raw RPC socket in an authenticated (HMAC-SHA256) proxy so you're not leaving an open port on the network. It's the RPC backend you just set up, minus the babysitting, under AGPL-3.0 so it can't be fenced off later." The "RPC backend you just set up" is upstream llama.cpp (Step 1: git clone https://github.com/ggerganov/llama.cpp.git; cmake -DGGML_RPC=ON; build targets rpc-server and llama-server), so the claim's paraphrase "around stock llama.cpp rpc-server and llama-server" and the inference that SharedLLM coordinates llama.cpp RPC workers rather than shipping its own sharding engine are supported. Only caveat: "stock" is the dossier's wording, not the post's, but it follows directly from the build instructions. Claim stands as of the 2026-07-18 version.

Fetched the cited URL (https://sharedllm.org/blog/sharedllm-vs-petals-vs-exo.html). It is primary: hosted on the project's own site, author self-identifies as "the person building SharedLLM", dated 2026-04-11, and states "this is v0.1.0 alpha". Every quoted sentence appears verbatim: "Only the tiny stories260K test model is verified end-to-end cross-container; larger quantized models hit a known upstream llama.cpp RPC assertion on certain tensor shapes (tracked, with a fix in flight upstream)." and "If you need a production-grade mesh today, SharedLLM is not that project." Governance text matches: "AGPL-3.0-or-later" (comparison table and footer), "Non-profit governance under the Developer Certificate of Origin (no CLA)", and "The DCO-not-CLA stance means the project can't be unilaterally relicensed". Corroborated by the same-day v0.1.0 announcement post (https://sharedllm.org/blog/announcing-sharedllm-v0-1-0.html), which repeats the identical stories260K/RPC-assertion statement (adding "a 4-bit row count that isn't a multiple of 512") and "Contributions are accepted under the Developer Certificate of Origin, not a CLA." Version scoping is correct: the site's Writing index lists no release newer than v0.1.0 as of 2026-08-22, and sharedllm.org/install.sh still defaults to VERSION=v0.1.0. Caveats for the dossier (not refutations, since the claim says "claimed"): the GitHub repo the source links (github.com/MHASK/sharedllm) returns 404 today, so LICENSE/GOVERNANCE.md cannot be verified from code; and the homepage attributes the project to "Naridon, Inc." ("© 2026 Naridon, Inc. All rights reserved", "At Cost, Not for Profit"), so "non-profit" is an unverified self-description, not a confirmed legal status.

Two of the three clauses hold, but the middle clause is false as stated. Verified 2026-08-22: (1) https://github.com/MHASK/sharedllm returns HTTP 404 on github.com and https://api.github.com/repos/MHASK/sharedllm returns 404 {"message":"Not Found"} -- confirmed; sharedllm.org home, /chat, /blog/ and blog posts all link to it (plus /blob/master/docs/install.md and /releases/latest, also 404) -- confirmed. (3) PyPI: https://pypi.org/pypi/sharedllm/json returns 404 and https://pypi.org/simple/sharedllm/ returns 404 -- supported (the literal /pypi/sharedllm URL 301-redirects to /project/sharedllm/, which sits behind a PyPI "Client Challenge" page, so the JSON/simple endpoints are the reliable check). (2) REFUTED: the GitHub REST search https://api.github.com/search/repositories?q=sharedllm returns 5 results, one of which is a public repository belonging to the project: MHASK/sharedllm-releases (same owner MHASK = Muhammed Ashique Kuthini; description "SharedLLM desktop app -- public release binaries (CDN-served). Source: private repo."; created 2026-06-08). Its README states "Source code lives in the private MHASK/sharedllm repo. This repo holds binaries only" and links to https://sharedllm.org. It carries releases v0.1.0 (2026-06-08), v0.2.0 and v0.2.1 (2026-06-10), each with SharedLLM-<ver>-aarch64.dmg / .app.tar.gz (macOS Apple Silicon only, Developer-ID signed, not notarized). This also corrects the implicit inference: the source repo is private, not deleted/nonexistent. The other 4 search hits (Clement25/SharedLLM, JMiahMan1/SharedLLM, Aakash80720/SharedLLM, Abhishek7424/sharedLLM) are unrelated projects.
